findings.title: FreeBSD
findings.replay_cell: xev selects kqueue, but the kqueue API is macOS-only and real consumers cannot type-check

vet.deferral_ref: .port/phase-2/XEV_BLUEPRINT.md:514 ("keep the FreeBSD posix.Kevent fast-path cfg-gated for later") and :519-521 ("cfg-gating discipline. Everything is #[cfg(target_os=\"macos\")]... other backends ported later as whole backends"); no FreeBSD row in DEFERRALS.md itself
vet.evidence: Reproduced on current main. Selector: crates/rustty-xev/src/backend.rs:48-50 default() returns Backend::Kqueue for freebsd; :101-103 candidates()=&[Kqueue] — faithful to oracle ghostty/zig-pkg/libxev-.../src/backend.zig:20,38 (.freebsd => .kqueue). But the real kqueue impl is macOS-gated: lib.rs:187-189 `#[cfg(target_os="macos")] mod kqueue;` and lib.rs:290-306 the whole `pub use kqueue::{...}` re-export block is cfg(macos). FreeBSD falls into no_backend_seam (lib.rs:611-617, cfg not macos/linux/windows/wasi), which defines only empty Loop/Async/Completion/Timer/Process/Stream/WriteRequest/WriteQueue with unimplemented!() (lib.rs:634-702) — no Options, RunMode, CallbackAction, CompletionState, WaitError, ProcessWaitError, TimerRunError, WriteBuffer, WriteError. rustty-termio consumes exactly those names (grep of crates/rustty-termio/src: xev::Options, xev::RunMode, xev::CallbackAction, xev::CompletionState, xev::WaitError, xev::ProcessWaitError, xev::TimerRunError, xev::WriteBuffer, xev::WriteError via xev_seam.rs:19 `pub use rustty_xev::*`), so a FreeBSD build fails name resolution at compile time. Oracle's kqueue backend genuinely supports FreeBSD: backend/kqueue.zig:35 `.freebsd => true` (available), :47 NOTE.EXIT freebsd arm, :1863 `.freebsd => std.c.Kevent`. Divergence is real: Ghostty type-checks and runs on FreeBSD; Rustty cannot.
vet.severity_assessment: Agree it is a real compile-time API-surface divergence, but P1 overstates practical impact: FreeBSD is deferred by the locked macOS-first plan, so this is planned whole-backend work, not a regression in a supported target.
vet.notes: Report is accurate and current (not stale). Remediation is not surgical: FreeBSD kqueue needs the cfg-gated kevent (vs kevent64_s) path, a non-mach Async wakeup, freebsd NOTE.EXIT semantics, and de-macOS-gating the module tree plus watcher instantiations — whole-backend platform work, hence fixable_now=false. Making backend.rs stop claiming Kqueue on freebsd would be anti-parity (oracle backend.zig maps freebsd→kqueue) and is not a fix. Member nuances: (1) iOS shares the identical mismatch — backend.rs:48 includes ios in the Kqueue arm while all kqueue modules are cfg(macos)-only; (2) rustty's freebsd/ios cfg arm omits visionos, which oracle backend.zig:19,37 includes; (3) W4-01's correction is right: the failure is deterministic compile-time name resolution (missing re-exports), not merely runtime unimplemented!() panics — the seam's placeholder structs cover only 8 of the ~19 names termio uses.

fix.detail:
Implemented §A (WI-1) + all of §B (WI-2..WI-8) of .port/codex-vet/designs/W2D_FREEBSD.md. FreeBSD now compiles the real kqueue backend instead of falling into `no_backend_seam`.

WI-1 (/Users/gael/projects/rustty/crates/rustty-os/src/pty.rs): `libc::IUTF8` has no freebsd binding, so a crate-local shim sits next to the use site — `#[cfg(not(freebsd))] use libc::IUTF8;` / `#[cfg(freebsd)] const IUTF8: libc::tcflag_t = 0x0000_4000;` — and `open()` now ORs the unqualified `IUTF8`. Value re-verified live this session: `curl 'https://cgit.freebsd.org/src/plain/sys/sys/_termios.h?h=releng/14.3' | grep IUTF8` → `#define IUTF8 0x00004000` (line 100).

WI-2 (kqueue.rs ABI core), all re-derived by content, not line number: `Kevent` split (`libc::kevent64_s` / `libc::kevent`); `kevent_init` grew the freebsd zeroed-init arm that never NAMES `ext` (so a freebsd11-ABI build still checks); a second `kevent_syscall` over plain `kevent(2)` with the identical errno map and `c_int` Overflow guard; `NOTE_EXIT_FLAGS` split (macOS `NOTE_EXIT|NOTE_EXITSTATUS`, freebsd `NOTE_EXIT` — libc has no freebsd `NOTE_EXITSTATUS`). findings.title: Terminal getter normal behavior matched, but `terminal_get_multi` selector arrays bypass raw C selector validation before Rust enum materialization and invalid direct getter diagnostics bypass Ghostty's C ABI log callback route
findings.replay_cell: independently upheld with severity correction for W35-B08-02

vet.evidence: Reproduced on main d34cc154. (B08-01) rustty_terminal_get validates raw c_int via terminal_data_from_c_int (lib.rs:1216-1223, 2649-2661), but rustty_terminal_get_multi (lib.rs:2670-2679) takes keys: *const terminal::TerminalData and forwards straight to terminal::get_multi, which loads `let key = unsafe { *keys.add(i) }` as a Rust enum with no raw check (terminal.rs:2547-2549) — an out-of-range C value is instant language-level UB in ANY Rust build profile. Oracle (ghostty @6ad1fe7d): get_multi loops through guarded get (terminal.zig:925-943), whose runtime_safety block std.enums.fromInt rejects invalid raw values → .invalid_value + failing index (terminal.zig:908-912). Same unguarded pattern persists in render/cell/row get_multi (lib.rs:1992-2000, 2108-2116, 2222-2230, 1107-1115) — W34-B02 kin, also unfixed. (B08-02) lib.rs:2657 eprintln! writes invalid-selector diagnostic straight to stderr; Ghostty C-ABI installs sys.zig logFn (lib_vt.zig:377-381) which is silent with no callback (sys.zig:188 `if (global.log == null) return`). Rustty HAS the mirror sys::log_fn (sys.rs:371-400, same silent-drop) but the wrapper bypasses it; systemic — 14 more eprintln! sites (lib.rs:113…2657). No deferral: grep of DEFERRALS/MAIN_PARITY/INTEGRATION_PARITY/GAP_ANALYSIS.md finds nothing for W35-B08/get_multi.
vet.fix_plan: (1) lib.rs rustty_terminal_get_multi: change Rust-side keys param to *const c_int (C header keeps `const TerminalData *keys` — same ABI, enum is int-sized); replicate get_multi's loop in the wrapper (or add a raw-keyed terminal::get_multi_raw): null keys/values -> InvalidValue; per element, terminal_data_from_c_int(k[i]) else { log-warn diag; *out_written=i if non-null; return InvalidValue } then terminal::get; preserve out_written=count on success. Behavioral delta vs oracle: invalid raw selector in array returns invalid_value with failing index (Ghostty safety-checked semantics) instead of UB. (2) Replace eprintln! at lib.rs:2657 with sys::log_fn(Warn, "", format_args!("terminal_get invalid data value={data}")) so it's callback-routed and silent by default (apply same to sibling sites under their own finding ids). Proving test: unit test in rustty-vt-c building a [c_int;3] = [0, 99, 1], calling rustty_terminal_get_multi via cast pointer, asserting InvalidValue and out_written==1; plus a test that valid arrays still succeed (existing get_multi_success stays green). Oracle has no such test (its guard is comptime-safety); adding one is allowed per task rules.
vet.severity_assessment: Agree: P1 for B08-01 (Rust invalid-enum materialization is unconditional UB, worse than oracle's safety-gated guard); agree with the P2->P4 correction for B08-02 (diagnostic-only routing divergence).
vet.notes: B08-01 is real UB-class but latent: it only fires when an embedder passes an out-of-range selector; well-behaved callers are unaffected. The report is accurate; one framing nuance — Ghostty ReleaseFast (safety off) is equally UB, so the parity gap is specifically vs safety-checked oracle builds, but Rust's unconditional UB still justifies P1. B08-02 is one instance of a systemic pattern: all 15 invalid-selector diagnostics in lib.rs use eprintln! instead of sys::log_fn; fixing only lib.rs:2657 closes this row, but the same one-line change should be batch-applied under the dedupe rows (W34-B02-02, W35-B03-DIAG-01, etc.). Registry INDEX.md:488-490 already records independent upholding with the severity correction; my audit agrees with that disposition.

fix.detail: B08-01 (the UB): moved the TerminalData narrowing out of lib.rs into terminal::TerminalData::from_c_int (hole-list mechanism preserved verbatim) and added terminal::get_checked(terminal, data: c_int, out) carrying the guard + log.warn. terminal::get_multi now takes keys: *const c_int and calls get_checked per element, so an out-of-range C selector yields InvalidValue + the failing index in out_written instead of materializing an invalid Rust enum. lib.rs wrapper keeps `*const TerminalData` (header unchanged: `const TerminalData *keys`) and casts. This follows the idiom W34-B02 already established for render. B08-02: the terminal_get diagnostic now goes through sys::log_fn. Negative control: neutering the range check makes the new tests abort with "trying to construct an enum from an invalid value 0x7a6a" (SIGABRT) — the exact UB the finding describes. Sibling cell/row/selection_gesture get_multi arrays left to W83-B01/W84-B01/W66-GETMULTI-RAW-01.

findings.title: FreeBSD/other non-Linux POSIX shared VT page allocator is compiled under broad non-wasm cfgs but defines `MAP_PRIVATE`/`MAP_ANONYMOUS` only for macOS/Linux, while Ghostty's non-Windows page allocator uses `std.posix.mmap` rather than a Linux-only constant table
findings.replay_cell: primary reviewed and coordinator replayed; FreeBSD full check was blocked by missing target/sysroot/C headers, but source cfg predicate and wasm countercheck were verified

vet.evidence: Reproduced on current main (d34cc15, post-dc054bb). crates/rustty-vt/src/page.rs: alloc/free/externs/PROT_*/MAP_FAILED are all gated only #[cfg(not(target_arch="wasm32"))] (lines 253, 276, 286-289, 300, 303), and alloc uses unqualified `MAP_PRIVATE | MAP_ANONYMOUS` at page.rs:261 — but MAP_PRIVATE/MAP_ANONYMOUS are defined only under cfg(target_os="macos") (291-294: 0x0002/0x1000) and cfg(target_os="linux") (295-298: 0x0002/0x0020). Any other non-wasm target (FreeBSD/NetBSD/OpenBSD/DragonFly) compiles the allocator with unresolved constants → E0425 compile break in shared VT core. Oracle: ghostty/src/terminal/page.zig:36 `else => AllocPosix`, and AllocPosix (page.zig:41-56) calls std.posix.mmap with symbolic flags, portable to all POSIX targets — the oracle is not macOS/Linux-only. The in-file PORT NOTE (page.rs:241-243) defers only the Windows AllocWindows variant; the comment at 283-285 ("signatures are stable across the platforms we target") does not cover the missing flag constants. Deferral docs checked: DEFERRALS.md has no FreeBSD entry (only wasm mmap→alloc_zeroed at :5456 and Windows spawn stubs); XEV_BLUEPRINT.md:514 defers only the FreeBSD Kevent fast-path in xev. No doc defers FreeBSD in shared VT page code. Primary report wave-60-b01-primary.md:52-91 matches my reading; its FreeBSD cargo check was toolchain-blocked, mine is source-predicate too.
vet.fix_plan: File: /Users/gael/projects/rustty/crates/rustty-vt/src/page.rs. Behavioral delta vs oracle: make the POSIX allocator compile on all non-wasm POSIX targets like Ghostty's AllocPosix (std.posix.mmap). Minimal surgical fix keeping the no-libc-dep design: replace the two per-OS constant pairs with grouped cfgs — #[cfg(any(target_os="macos", target_os="freebsd", target_os="netbsd", target_os="openbsd", target_os="dragonfly"))] MAP_PRIVATE=0x0002, MAP_ANONYMOUS=0x1000 (all BSD-lineage kernels use MAP_ANON=0x1000); keep #[cfg(any(target_os="linux", target_os="android"))] MAP_PRIVATE=0x0002, MAP_ANONYMOUS=0x0020. Proving tests: (1) add a host unit test asserting page_alloc::{MAP_PRIVATE,MAP_ANONYMOUS} == libc::{MAP_PRIVATE,MAP_ANON} (libc as dev-dependency only), which proves value parity on every platform the suite ever runs on; (2) `rustup target add x86_64-unknown-freebsd` (tier-2 rust-std) then `cargo check -p rustty-vt --target x86_64-unknown-freebsd` as the compile-coverage probe — if C -sys deps in the dependency graph still block before page.rs (as the primary observed), fall back to an isolated rustc --emit=metadata probe of the page module cfg arms, and record the residual dep-level FreeBSD blockers under the existing F-00x family rather than this finding.
vet.severity_assessment: Agree it is a real compile-breaking gap in shared VT core; P1 is fair within the non-macOS lane, though impact is latent since whole-app FreeBSD is already blocked by canonical F-002/F-003/F-004.
vet.notes: Single-member group; the companion row W60-B01-DUP-F001-WINPAGE (no Windows VirtualAlloc port) is correctly deduped under canonical F-001, and the Windows deferral IS documented in-file (page.rs:241-243) — only the POSIX-constants gap is undocumented. Report is accurate; no corrections needed. Fix is plan-consistent: it is a few-line cfg/constant change in shared VT code, not platform-subsystem work.

fix.detail: crates/rustty-vt/src/page.rs page_alloc: dropped the hand-rolled mmap/munmap externs and the macOS/Linux-only MAP_PRIVATE/MAP_ANONYMOUS/PROT_*/MAP_FAILED table; the allocator now calls libc::mmap/libc::munmap with libc::{PROT_READ,PROT_WRITE,MAP_PRIVATE,MAP_ANONYMOUS,MAP_FAILED}. DEVIATION FROM FIX PLAN: the plan's 'keep the no-libc-dep design, add BSD cfg arms' rationale is stale — libc is already an unconditional dependency of rustty-vt (kitty/graphics_image uses libc::mmap/MAP_FAILED, rustty-os/page_allocator.rs uses libc::MAP_PRIVATE|MAP_ANON). Sourcing the flags from libc is the exact Rust analog of the oracle's symbolic std.posix.mmap (page.zig:41-56) and is correct on every POSIX target, with no per-OS value table to get wrong (it also fixes the hardcoded i64 offset on 32-bit targets). PORT NOTE rewritten to record the old gap. Proof: isolated page_alloc module compiled for x86_64-unknown-freebsd — BEFORE: error[E0425] cannot find value MAP_PRIVATE / MAP_ANONYMOUS; AFTER: clean. Whole-crate `cargo check -p rustty-vt --target x86_64-unknown-freebsd` is still blocked earlier by highway-sys C++ cross-compile (no FreeBSD sysroot) — the pre-existing F-00x dep-level blocker, not p

findings.replay_cell: VT callback table is private, so browser embedders cannot install effect callbacks

vet.evidence: Reproduced myself on current main (d34cc15; only commit since audit pin dc054bb is "untrack codex stuff" — no source change). (1) Oracle: /Users/gael/projects/ghostty/src/build/GhosttyLibVt.zig:56 sets `exe.export_table = true` ("so that embedders (e.g. JS in a browser) can insert callback entries"), then runs wasm_patch_growable_table and installs the patched ghostty-vt.wasm (lines 61-85). (2) Rustty: .port/tools/build-vt-wasm.sh:13-15 is a plain `cargo build -p rustty-vt-c --target wasm32-unknown-unknown --release` — no --export-table link-arg, no patch step; it self-describes as "the rustty analog of ghostty's ghostty-vt.wasm". No .cargo/config.toml, no build.rs in rustty-vt-c, grep for export-table/rustflags across repo: none. The ported patcher (xtask/src/wasm_patch_growable_table.rs, main.rs:514-528) is manual-only and by design changes only limits, not exports. (3) I ran the build script and .port/codex/scripts/inspect-wasm-table.mjs on the fresh artifact: tableExports:[], imports:[], table flags:1 min:212 max:212 — private, non-growable, zero imports, so JS has no path to install the fn-pointer callbacks that rustty_sys_set accepts (crates/rustty-vt-c/src/lib.rs:389-400; sys.rs:255-280 transmutes value to DecodePngFn/LogFn — on wasm these are table indices). (4) No deferral: DEFERRALS.md:5459-5461 records the patcher as ported "mirrors the table-patch step of GhosttyLibVt.initWasm" but never defers the export_table wiring; WS14 plan line 58 marks the area "present".
vet.fix_plan: Mirror GhosttyLibVt.initWasm's three-step contract in .port/tools/build-vt-wasm.sh: (a) build with the table exported — `cargo rustc -p rustty-vt-c --target wasm32-unknown-unknown --release -- -C link-arg=--export-table` (rust-lld exports `__indirect_function_table`); (b) run the already-ported patcher `cargo run -p xtask -- wasm-patch-growable-table target/.../rustty_vt_c.wasm <out>/rustty-vt.wasm` to drop the table max (faithful to ghostty's patch step; alternatively `-C link-arg=--growable-table` since wasm-ld supports it, but the patcher path matches the oracle pipeline and finally exercises the ported code); (c) emit the installed artifact as `rustty-vt.wasm` (analog of ghostty-vt.wasm) and point the wasm examples at it. Behavioral delta vs oracle: module gains exported growable funcref table `__indirect_function_table` (flags 0, max null), enabling JS to table.grow/set a callback and pass its index to rustty_sys_set(DecodePng/Log). Proving test: extend .port/tools/wasm-parity.mjs (node) to assert on the built module that WebAssembly.Module.exports includes a table export, instantiate it, assert `instance.exports.__indirect_function_table.grow(1)` succeeds (throws today on the bounded table), and that rustty_sys_set(2, idx) returns success for a table index — run via the existing wasm parity lane.
vet.severity_assessment: Agree P2: the advertised browser VT artifact structurally breaks the public C-ABI callback contract (PNG decode, log), though no in-repo wasm example consumes it yet.
vet.notes: Single member row F-006; INDEX row 31 correctly separates it from W16-CABI-01 (type_json memory-growth) and W12-05 (metadata deltas). One report nuance: the patcher is not merely "manually invoked" — it is wired to no build path at all (grep of .port/tools, Makefile, .github found zero call sites). Also note wasm-ld does support --growable-table, so ghostty's "linker doesn't support it" comment is Zig-linker-specific; Rustty may pick either mechanism without fidelity loss, but should still export the table either way.

findings.title: Default Linux build
findings.replay_cell: Neither native Wayland nor X11 integration is enabled by default

vet.evidence: Reproduced on current main (d34cc154). crates/rustty/Cargo.toml:36-44: `default = ["gtk"]`; `wayland`/`x11` are opt-in pass-throughs, comment explicitly says "OFF by default ... a plain `--features gtk` build stays noop-only". crates/rustty-apprt/src/gtk/winproto.rs:23-32,122-145: without those features only the noop arm compiles and App::init always lands on App::None. PACKAGING.md:104-112 (documented Linux package build) runs `cargo build --offline --locked --release -p rustty` with no feature flags. Oracle: ghostty src/build/gtk.zig:9-27 probes `pkg-config --variable=targets gtk4`; src/build/Config.zig:208-218 defaults gtk-wayland/gtk-x11 from that probe — on a normal distro GTK both default ON. Probes I ran: `cargo tree -p rustty -e features --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu | grep -c 'gdk4-wayland|gdk4-x11|wayland-client'` = 0 (exit 1); with `--features wayland,x11` = 18 (exit 0). So both arms are fully implemented (winproto/{wayland.rs,x11.rs} exist; DEFERRALS.md:5891-5945 records both landed and live-VM-verified) but a default/documented Linux build compiles neither. No deferral doc records the default-off as a deferral; the Cargo.toml comment frames it as deliberate design expecting distros to opt in, and rustty-apprt Cargo.toml:288+ puts all protocol deps in the cfg(target_os="linux") table, so default-on would be a no-op off Linux (same pattern as `gtk`).
vet.fix_plan: Two-part, surgical: (1) crates/rustty/Cargo.toml — change `default = ["gtk"]` to `default = ["gtk", "wayland", "x11"]`, updating the feature comment. Safe off-Linux: every protocol dep lives in rustty-apprt's [target.'cfg(target_os = "linux")'.dependencies] table (Cargo.toml:288-370) and all code is #[cfg(all(target_os="linux", feature=...))]-gated, so macOS/embedded builds are byte-identical (same mechanism already proven for the default-on `gtk` feature). Cargo cannot replicate Ghostty's pkg-config autodetection (src/build/gtk.zig:9-27) declaratively; default-on with a documented opt-out (`--no-default-features --features gtk[,wayland|,x11]` for single-target GTK builds) is the closest analogue and matches Ghostty's effective default on normal distro GTK (both targets on). (2) PACKAGING.md — note the default now includes both arms and document the opt-out for wayland-only/x11-only GTK installs. Proving test: a gate script (e.g. .port/tools/gates/) or xtask test asserting `cargo tree -p rustty -e features --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` contains gdk4-wayland, gdk4-x11, and wayland-client with default features, and that the macOS default graph contains none — the exact probe pair used in this audit, inverted for the Linux arm.
vet.severity_assessment: Agree with P2: default Linux package silently loses SSD decorations, blur, urgency, quick terminal, WINDOWID — but GTK still launches, so no higher.
vet.notes: W2-04 correctly folded into F-007; the independent review's High->P2 correction is sound (noop arm is not a GUI launch failure — GTK's own backend still connects to the display). Report is accurate on current main; nothing already fixed. The off-by-default is documented deliberate DESIGN in the Cargo.toml comment ("A Linux distro build enables the arms its target sessions need — typically both"), but no deferral/parity doc registers the resulting divergence from Ghostty's pkg-config-derived defaults, so known_deferred=false. One fix caveat: default-on x11/wayland assumes distro GTK built with both targets (the very case Ghostty's pkg-config probe guards); the opt-out path must stay documented for single-target GTK builds.

fix.detail: default = ["gtk","wayland","x11"] in crates/rustty/Cargo.toml with pkg-config-analogue rationale + opt-out comment; PACKAGING.md Build Options documents the single-target GTK opt-out. Proving gate check_default_linux_winproto.sh runs the audit's exact cargo-tree probe pair (Linux default: all 3 protocol crates present; macOS default: none) with anti-vacuity rustty-apprt checks; verified FAIL on old default, PASS on new. macOS no-op confirmed via cargo check -p rustty. Actual Linux GUI build: linux-ci-verification-pending.
fix.tests_run: cargo test -p xtask: 38 passed, 0 failed, 2 ignored. cargo test -p xtask dist_tarball_ships_vendor_inputs -- --ignored: 1 passed, 0 failed. .port/tools/gates/check_default_linux_winproto.sh: PASS (and verified FAIL with the pre-fix default via revert-run-restore). cargo check -p rustty: clean. cargo clippy -p xtask -- -D warnings: clean. Smoke: cargo run -p xtask -- resources (macOS default, no linux dirs) and -- resources --target-os linux --prefix /usr (all 7 asset dirs staged, desktop file substituted).

findings.title: C ABI
findings.replay_cell: `rustty_terminal_new` ignores caller-supplied allocator

vet.evidence: Reproduced on current main (d34cc15; `git log dc054bb..HEAD -- crates/rustty-vt-c/src/terminal.rs` is empty, so unchanged since the audit pin). Rustty: crates/rustty-vt-c/src/lib.rs:2476 `rustty_terminal_new` -> terminal::new -> new_ (crates/rustty-vt-c/src/terminal.rs:953). terminal.rs:967 resolves the caller allocator into `let _alloc = rustty_lib::allocator::default(alloc_);` and DISCARDS it; :968 uses `allocator_api2::alloc::Global` for ZigTerminal::init; :1009 and :1062 heap-box terminal and wrapper via `Box::into_raw` on the Rust global heap; :1054 + :79 back the stream/OSC with process-static `GLOBAL_ZIG_ALLOCATOR_FOR_OSC`; free reclaims via `Box::from_raw` (:2774, :2807). rustty-lib's `default` genuinely honors a non-null caller allocator (crates/rustty-lib/src/allocator.rs:125-128), so the bypass is entirely in new_. Oracle: ghostty src/terminal/c/terminal.zig:398-465 `new_` does `lib.alloc.default(alloc_)` then `alloc.create` for ZigTerminal, TerminalWrapper, and io_impl, threads `alloc` into `t.init` and `stream=.initAlloc(alloc,handler)`, and returns recoverable `error.OutOfMemory`; `free` (:1103-1119) recovers the allocator via `t.gpa()` and `alloc.destroy`s all three. Net: caller arenas/quotas/fault-injection are silently bypassed; a rejecting caller allocator still succeeds via the Rust global heap, and real OOM aborts instead of returning RUSTTY_OUT_OF_MEMORY.
vet.fix_plan: Surgical boundary fix in crates/rustty-vt-c/src/terminal.rs (+ small raw create/destroy helpers in crates/rustty-lib/src/allocator.rs if absent): (1) keep the resolved `Box<dyn ZigAllocator>` from `default(alloc_)` and store it (or a ZigAllocatorRef-able owner) in TerminalWrapper; (2) allocate the ZigTerminal and TerminalWrapper storage through that allocator's raw alloc with the types' Layouts instead of `Box::into_raw` on Global, mapping rejection to recoverable `NewError::OutOfMemory` (matching oracle new_ terminal.zig:405-412); (3) pass the stored allocator to `Stream::init_alloc(...)` in place of `GLOBAL_ZIG_ALLOCATOR_FOR_OSC` (oracle: `.initAlloc(alloc, handler)`); (4) `free` deallocates terminal+wrapper through the stored allocator, mirroring oracle free's `t.gpa()` recovery (terminal.zig:1103-1119). Behavioral delta: caller-supplied allocator observes/owns wrapper-level lifecycle allocations, and a rejecting allocator makes rustty_terminal_new return RUSTTY_OUT_OF_MEMORY with *result=null instead of silently succeeding on the global heap. Proving test (rustty-vt-c unit test, oracle has lib.alloc.test_allocator equivalents): a counting C allocator vtable sees >0 allocs during rustty_terminal_new and balances to 0 after rustty_terminal_free; an always-rejecting allocator yields RUSTTY_OUT_OF_MEMORY, null handle, no abort. Residual honestly out of surgical scope: rustty-vt hardwires `Global as Allocator` (crates/rustty-vt/src/terminal.rs:94), so internal screen/pagelist allocations still bypass the caller allocator; full oracle parity (caller allocator driving all terminal internals, per `t.init(...,alloc,...)`) requires making rustty-vt runtime-allocator-polymorphic — a structural cross-crate project, tracked by the W12-01 extension rows.
vet.severity_assessment: Agree P2: real shared C-ABI contract divergence on every platform's embedder surface, though the macOS app path (default/null allocator) is unaffected, so not higher.
vet.notes: Not an unnoticed bug: the divergence is a deliberate, in-code-documented decision — terminal.rs:946-952 port note says wrapper/terminal storage go on the Rust global heap "per the signed-off D3 storage plan", and NEXT_PHASE_PLAN.md Stage B records D3 as signed off. However, no DEFERRALS.md/MAIN_PARITY.md/GAP_ANALYSIS.md row records the caller-allocator bypass, and it is not a macOS-first platform deferral (it affects macOS embedders too), so known_deferred=false. Member-row nuance: F-008 is canonical only for terminal_new; W12-01/W34/W35/W66/W90 rows are dedup'd affected units (other constructors, render/selection, tracked grid refs — e.g. terminal.rs:2681 TrackedGridRef Box::into_raw) and would need the same treatment; W36-B06 correctly notes the allocator convenience wrappers themselves DO honor the supplied allocator, and W87-B03 shows formatter format_alloc honors it — the bypass is lifecycle-specific, exactly as the report scoped it. One report imprecision: 'graceful OOM reporting' bypass matters only under real memory pressure or fault-injecting allocators; with a rejecting caller allocator Rustty succeeds (bypass) rather than crashing.

fix.detail: rustty_terminal_new/free now route wrapper-level lifecycle through the caller C allocator per oracle terminal.zig new_/free: create_raw/destroy_raw helpers (rustty-lib) allocate ZigTerminal + TerminalWrapper storage via the resolved allocator with oracle OOM ordering (create t, create wrapper, init) and errdefer unwinds; rejecting allocator yields RUSTTY_OUT_OF_MEMORY + null; OSC stream is initAlloc(alloc,...) backed by the wrapper-held allocator (raw-ptr holder to avoid Box retag SB UB, reclaimed last in free); free returns both storages through the caller allocator. Miri-clean. Tier-2 residual (Terminal internals on Global) recorded in DEFERRALS.md.
fix.tests_run: cargo test -p rustty-lib → 16 passed / 0 failed; cargo test -p rustty-vt-c → 379 passed / 0 failed (was 366 pre-batch; +13 proving tests); cargo test -p rustty-vt-c terminal::tests::new_ → 4/0; cargo test -p rustty-vt-c allocator:: → 7/0; cargo +nightly miri test -p rustty-vt-c (new lifecycle + vt_write + allocator tests) → 22 passed / 0 failed; fail-first: git stash of render.rs → render_new_free_uses_caller_allocator + render_new_rejecting_allocator_out_of_memory FAILED pre-fix, pass post-fix; cargo check -p rustty-vt -p rustty-apprt-api -p rustty-renderer -p rustty-inspector -p rustty-termi

Oracle ghostty/src/apprt/gtk/class/application.zig:603-644 constructs `CloseConfirmationDialog.new(.app)`, connects close-request → handleCloseConfirmation (:1552-1557, calls quitNow), and presents. The blocker no longer exists: close_confirmation_dialog.rs:177-190 has `new(Target)`/`present(Option<&Widget>)`, Target::App strings at :59,:71, and Window close already wires the identical pattern (window.rs:1749-1769). vet.evidence: Reproduced on current main (d34cc15). Rustty: crates/rustty-apprt/src/gtk/class/application.rs:2874-2895 quit_now() keeps the loop over gtk4::Window::list_toplevels() and the fcitx comment, but the body is `let _ = window;` (:2890) — no isA guard, no destroy — then sets running=false (:2894). quit() at :2851-2853 routes non-confirming quits there, so the widget/tab/surface/core-surface finalization cascade never runs. The placeholder note (:2884-2889) claims dormancy "until Task 12 lands (no Window toplevels exist)" — stale: the Window subclass is fully landed (window.rs:218 ObjectSubclass impl, :1487 wrapper) and instantiated live (application.rs:3572 Window::new in the new-window action; :3342-3343 windows() downcasts toplevels to Window). Proving test: alongside the existing run-loop test at application.rs:~4893 (which already asserts quit_now clears running), add a gtk test (pattern of tests/gtk_close_confirmation.rs) that builds the test app, creates a Window via Window::new, calls quit_now, and asserts (a) list_toplevels no longer yields any Window downcast (destroy ran) and (b) running is false. findings.title: Linux GTK
findings.replay_cell: Captured launch-time `LANG` is discarded from child environments

vet.evidence: Reproduced on current main (d34cc154; report's cited files unchanged since dc054bb). Ghostty oracle: launch LANG snapshotted before config.language override (ghostty/src/apprt/gtk/class/application.zig:279-290), savedLanguage returns the stored value (:475-478), defaultTermioEnv puts it back into the child env, removing LANG only if absent at launch (ghostty/src/apprt/gtk/class/surface.zig:1602-1606). Rustty: capture+override ARE ported (crates/rustty-apprt/src/gtk/class/application.rs:2295-2303 via env_getenv->Option<Vec<u8>>, :5233), stored in imp.saved_language (:189, :2402), freed at deinit (:1883-1885) — but the sole accessor saved_language() returns literal None (:2206-2208), so the only consumer default_termio_env always takes the removal arm (crates/rustty-apprt/src/gtk/class/surface.rs:2354-2360), stripping launch LANG from every default GTK child env; termio overlays config.env after (crates/rustty-termio/src/exec.rs:2212-2221), so an explicit env=LANG=... can mask it (W3-01 correction verified). grep confirms saved_language() has exactly one production call (surface.rs:2354). The accessor's doc comment (:2201-2204) marks it "Placeholder-leaf (language-override tier)" claiming the capture "lands with that work" — stale: the capture already landed, only the accessor was never unstubbed.
vet.deferral_ref: In-code only: crates/rustty-apprt/src/gtk/class/application.rs:2201-2204 placeholder-leaf note ("language-override tier"). Not recorded in .port/phase-2/DEFERRALS.md, MAIN_PARITY.md, INTEGRATION_PARITY.md, or GAP_ANALYSIS.md (grep negative); PREPORT_GTK.md:41 covers only the field's ownership discipline. The note's stated precondition (LANG capture landing) is already satisfied, so the deferral rationale is obsolete.
vet.fix_plan: 1) crates/rustty-apprt/src/gtk/class/application.rs:2206-2208 — replace `None` with a read of the stored field: `self.imp().saved_language.borrow().clone()` returning Option<CString> (change signature from Option<String>; CString preserves the raw launch bytes, matching Zig ?[:0]const u8 per byte-fidelity doctrine), and drop the now-false placeholder comment. 2) crates/rustty-apprt/src/gtk/class/surface.rs:2354-2356 — adjust the Some arm to `language.to_bytes()`. Behavioral delta vs oracle: default child env keeps the launch-time LANG (post config.language override capture semantics identical to application.zig:279-290 + surface.zig:1602-1606); LANG removed only when absent at launch. Proof: Linux-gated unit test in the gtk application module — set imp.saved_language, assert saved_language() returns it and default_termio_env's map contains LANG=that value; plus a None-field test asserting LANG absent. Runs 0 tests on macOS host (like existing gtk_* binaries) but verifiable via aarch64-linux cross-check/CI; the static predicate rustty-saved-language-hardcoded-none in .port/codex/scripts/gtk-bsd/check_runtime_gaps.sh must be updated to expect the fixed shape.
vet.severity_assessment: Agree with corrected P2: material default-child-env locale loss on Linux GTK (not shipping-critical on macOS-first plan; user config.env can mask).
vet.notes: Member rows F-011 and W3-01 are the same root; W3-01's correction ("every child loses LANG" too absolute) is accurate — termio applies config.env after the default map. Report correction: the audit framed the accessor as awaiting the "language-override tier", but the capture/override/storage/deinit all already exist on main; the gap is a single unstubbed accessor, making this the cheapest confirmed fix in the GTK group. Negative control verified: when launch env lacks LANG, both implementations remove it — divergence requires LANG present at launch.

vet.evidence: Reproduced on current main (d34cc15, one bookkeeping commit past audit pin dc054bb; no code change). include/rustty/vt/render.h:100-111 declares RusttyRenderStateDirty with MAX_VALUE=RUSTTY_ENUM_MAX_VALUE (=INT_MAX, include/rustty/vt/types.h:69) → 4-byte int storage. (src/terminal/render.zig:266) whose C backing is c_int (src/lib/enum.zig:43 `.c => c_int`), so getTyped/setTyped (c/render.zig:263,335) move full 4 bytes. vet.severity_assessment: Agree with P2: public C-ABI correctness bug on the primary render-loop dirty query; get returns garbage high bytes to any C caller (including the shipped example), set has latent UB on low-byte transmute.
vet.notes: Member row W34-B03-001 is accurate as worded. findings.title: Shared-grid and glyph-fallback Fontconfig iterators leak their owned native pattern/font-set handles
findings.replay_cell: upheld with scope correction

vet.evidence: Reproduced on main (d34cc154; `git log dc054bb..HEAD -- crates/rustty-font-shaper/` empty, so unchanged since pin). Fontconfig DiscoverIterator (crates/rustty-font-shaper/src/discovery.rs:260-273) owns raw `*mut fc::Pattern` + `*mut fc::FontSet`; only cleanup is manual `deinit()` calling FcFontSetDestroy/FcPatternDestroy (discovery.rs:279-290). `grep -rn "impl Drop" crates/rustty-font-shaper/src/` hits only face/freetype.rs:1327 (BitmapGuard) — no Drop on iterator or fc wrappers. Leak sites never call deinit: shared_grid_set.rs:338 + 372 carry only `// defer disco_it.deinit(); — RAII scope drop` comments (RAII claim is false for raw ptrs); codepoint_resolver.rs:271 comment-only, all exits (return via add_deferred, break on error/exhaustion, break 'discover) skip deinit. Oracle: ghostty SharedGridSet.zig:197,228 and CodepointResolver.zig:182 have `defer disco_it.deinit()`. Scope corrections verified: CoreText iterator (discovery.rs:1845-1867) holds `Vec<CFRetained<CTFontDescriptor>>` — true RAII, so macOS unaffected; apple-emoji site shared_grid_set.rs:511 is cfg(macos)→CoreText; font_sort failure destroys pattern (discovery.rs:218-222); list_fonts.rs:363 deinits on normal completion. Module cfg'd off on macOS/windows/wasm (discovery.rs:92-99), so leak is Linux/BSD Fontconfig builds — un-deferred, verified live on Fedora per DEFERRALS.md:3155-3169 (struck-through deferral).
vet.fix_plan: In crates/rustty-font-shaper/src/discovery.rs fontconfig_impl: make `DiscoverIterator::deinit` idempotent (null out `set`/`pattern` after destroy) and add `impl Drop for DiscoverIterator { fn drop(&mut self) { self.deinit() } }`. This makes the existing "RAII scope drop" comments at shared_grid_set.rs:338/372 and the comment-only defer at codepoint_resolver.rs:271 true on every exit (success, miss, continue, `?` propagation), matching Ghostty's `defer disco_it.deinit()` (SharedGridSet.zig:197/228, CodepointResolver.zig:182). Safe because next() render-prepares an owned pattern for each DeferredFace, same as Zig. list_fonts.rs's explicit deinit stays valid via idempotence. Behavioral delta: FcPattern+FcFontSet destroyed once per iterator on all paths instead of leaked. Proof: add a cfg(all(not(macos),not(windows),not(wasm32))) unit test in discovery.rs asserting Drop runs deinit (e.g., discover a descriptor, drop the iterator, assert nulled/flagged state via a test-only counter), executed on the Fedora verification host used for the fontconfig un-deferral; on macOS, `cargo check --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu -p rustty-font-shaper` gates compilation.
vet.severity_assessment: Agree with P2: unbounded process-lifetime native leak per grid build and per glyph-fallback query on Linux/BSD builds; macOS unaffected.
vet.notes: Single-member group; report accurate including its scope corrections (list-fonts normal path and CoreText RAII correctly excluded). codepoint_resolver.rs:411-439 override path deinits on the two ordinary outcomes; its error-path gaps belong to W9F-02, not this group.

fix.detail: discovery.rs fontconfig_impl: deinit() made idempotent (nulls set/pattern after FcFontSetDestroy/FcPatternDestroy, clears the borrowed `fonts` vec + i so a post-deinit next() yields None instead of reading freed patterns) and added `impl Drop for DiscoverIterator { deinit() }`, so Ghostty's `defer disco_it.deinit()` (SharedGridSet.zig:197/228, CodepointResolver.zig:182) now holds on EVERY exit (?-propagation, break 'discover, early return). Existing explicit deinit() calls stay correct via idempotence. Stale PORT NOTE at codepoint_resolver.rs:271 ('DiscoverIterator has no Drop') corrected. linux-ci-verification-pending: module is cfg'd off on macOS and cross-check needs aarch64-linux-gnu-gcc (absent) — the exact Drop/idempotence/thread-local idiom was compiled and proven on an isolated rustc --test harness (/tmp/w9f01/idiom.rs: passes with Drop, FAILS without).

I reproduced the cross-check failure myself (cargo check --target aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu -p rustty-font-shaper --tests dies in cc-rs: 'failed to find tool aarch64-linux-gnu-gcc'). Mitigations I verified directly: (1) the exact idiom compiles and the test logic is delta-proving — I ran /tmp/w9f01/idiom.rs (passes) and /tmp/w9f01/nodrop.rs (identical minus impl Drop, FAILS), and it covers every at-risk construct (cfg(test) thread_local with const block, statement-level cfg attr, pub(super) access from the child tests module, Drop + idempotence); (2) the new test mirrors the adjacent already-compiling `fontconfig` test's idioms exactly (Descriptor derives Clone/Debug/Default; same Library/Fontconfig::init/deinit shape). Residual risk is a type/typo error in this module only, not a fidelity or design gap. Fedora/Linux CI must run `cargo test -p rustty-font-shaper discover_iterator_drops_native_handles` before this is closed.

vet.evidence: Reproduced on current main (d34cc15; uucode.rs untouched since audit pin dc054bb per git log). Rustty crates/rustty-font-shaper/src/uucode.rs:26 hand-embeds EMOJI_PRESENTATION as 289 ranges/1212 points; I parsed the tuple body and range-tested: all seven scalars U+1F6D8, U+1FA8A, U+1FA8E, U+1FAC8, U+1FACD, U+1FAEA, U+1FAEF fall in no range (containment check, not literal grep). Oracle: Ghostty pins uucode-0.2.0-ZZjBPlK5... (ghostty/build.zig.zon:49-52); its local package zig-pkg/uucode-0.2.0-ZZjBPlK5.../ucd/emoji/emoji-data.txt is "# Version: 17.0" (sha256 2cb2bb94..., matching the report's independently fetched archive) and lists all seven as Emoji_Presentation E17.0 (lines 650,715,716,730,731,741,742). My full set-difference: oracle 1219 pts, rust 1212, oracle_only = exactly those seven, rust_only empty. Consumer: codepoint_resolver.rs:215-222 computes PresentationMode::Default(Text) when uucode::is_emoji_presentation(cp) is false, so bare U17 default-emoji scalars request Text and the deferred-face presentation predicate can reject a capable color-emoji fallback (report's Fontconfig/Windows trace; source-level, not rerun here). (the version uucode 0.2.0 ships)" — factually wrong; uucode 0.2.0 ships Unicode 17.0 data, so this is a fidelity bug in the shim, not a version-choice deferral.

Fix the header comment (uucode.rs:17,24) from "Unicode 16.0.0" to "Unicode 17.0". Proving test: extend uucode::tests (near line 340) emoji_presentation_spot_checks with U17 controls asserting is_emoji_presentation == true for all seven (e.g. U+1FACD orca) plus a non-emoji neighbor control (e.g. U+1F6D9 false), and optionally assert total point count 1219. findings.title: Native CLI actions leak internal configuration reads to stderr despite the action logging gate
findings.replay_cell: upheld; scoped to config-loading actions

vet.evidence: Current main (d34cc154): crates/rustty-config/src/config_struct.rs:5311-5317 — log_info/log_warn are unconditional eprintln!("info(config): ...") with NO gate; :5792-5795 load_fs_file emits "reading configuration file path=..." on every file load; crates/rustty-cli/src/list_themes.rs:399-401 loads each theme via load_file, so list-themes emits one stderr line per theme. The action gate IS ported: rustty-apprt/src/lib.rs:96-110 compute_logging sets logging.stderr=false when an action is detected (RUSTTY_LOG override honored), and rustty-core/src/logging.rs:37-115 log_with/log honor logging.stderr — but apprt publishes the state only to rustty_core::STATE (lib.rs:354-357), and rustty-config CANNOT read it: rustty-core/Cargo.toml:29 depends on rustty-config (edge would cycle). rustty-global (which config depends on) holds a Logging type + STATE OnceLock (lib.rs:104,178) but apprt never sets it. Oracle: ghostty src/global.zig sets self.logging.stderr=false on action detection; main_ghostty.zig:155 logFn checks global.logging().stderr before every stderr write; Config.zig:3983 uses std.log.info → gated. Runtime reproduction: cargo test -p rustty-config handle_bom_in_config_files -- --nocapture printed "info(config): skipping UTF-8 byte order mark" to stderr (line :5827, same ungated helper). No deferral found; DEFERRALS.md:3414-3421 documents the bin logFn gate as LIVE and action stdout "clean", contradicting the actual config-crate bypass. The port comment at :5309-5310 ("go to stderr like the reference's scoped logger") misstates the reference contract.
vet.fix_plan: Host the logging state at the leaf the way the reference does (global.logging() is a free accessor on global state): (1) rustty-global/src/lib.rs — add a process-global gated accessor, e.g. `static LOGGING: OnceLock<Logging>` + `pub fn set_logging(Logging)` + `pub fn logging() -> Logging` defaulting to Logging::default() when unset (matches reference pre-init default of stderr=true). (2) rustty-apprt/src/lib.rs init_with_action — call rustty_global::set_logging(logging) right where state.logging is mirrored into rustty_core::STATE (~:355), keeping one computation site. (3) rustty-config/src/config_struct.rs log_info/log_warn (:5311-5317) — early-return unless rustty_global::logging().stderr, then eprintln as today; fix the :5309 comment. Behavioral delta vs oracle: with an action detected and no RUSTTY_LOG, config reads/warns produce zero stderr (Ghostty logFn skips when logging.stderr==false); RUSTTY_LOG=stderr re-enables, GUI/no-action path unchanged. Proving tests: rustty-global unit test for set_logging/logging default+set; rustty-config test that sets stderr=false via the new setter, runs load_reader on a BOM'd config (the handle_bom path), and asserts via a refactored `fn format_log(kind,msg, logging)->Option<String>` (single eprintln call site) that the gated variant returns None while default returns Some — avoiding fragile stderr capture. Optionally a rustty-cli list-themes smoke test asserting quiet stderr under the gate.
vet.severity_assessment: Agree with P3: stdout stays parseable and exit code is 0, but the action stderr contract (quiet by default) is genuinely broken for every config-loading action.
vet.notes: Single-member group; report's citations reproduce exactly on current main (unchanged since the dc054bb pin — only .port bookkeeping commits landed since). The independent review's refinements are correct: RUSTTY_LOG=no-stderr does not silence these lines (they bypass the parser entirely), and non-config actions (e.g. version) stay quiet. Structural root cause the report understates: this is not a forgotten call — rustty-config cannot reach the gated logger in rustty-core because rustty-core depends on rustty-config, so the fix requires hosting the logging state in the leaf crate rustty-global (which config already depends on, per its Cargo.toml comment "rustty-global is the LEAF state-holder"). Other leaf crates with direct eprintln! exist but are correctly out of this finding's scope.

fix.detail: Hosted the reference global.logging() gate at the leaf: rustty-global grew a LOGGING OnceLock mirror (set_logging/logging, default-when-unset); rustty-apprt init_with_action publishes the computed logging to it alongside rustty_core::STATE; rustty-config log_info/log_warn now gate via format_log(kind,msg,logging) early-returning None when !logging.stderr, comment fixed. Live-verified: `rustty +show-config` stderr has 0 info(config) lines; RUSTTY_LOG=stderr re-enables (2 lines). DEFERRALS.md stale NOTE struck. Optional list-themes CLI smoke test skipped (cli_smoke.rs outside batch file set).
fix.tests_run: cargo test -p rustty-global (10+1 passed, 0 failed); cargo test -p rustty-config --lib (204 passed, 0 failed, includes the 2 new gate tests + handle_bom_in_config_files); cargo test -p rustty-apprt --lib (12 passed, 0 failed, includes bootstrap_tests::compute_logging_*); cargo check -p rustty-cli and cargo check -p rustty both clean. Runtime KAT: target/debug/rustty +show-config → exit 0, stderr grep -c 'info(config)' = 0; RUSTTY_LOG=stderr variant = 2.

findings.title: public `type_json()` hides scroll-viewport/scrollbar field maps and labels one enum as `i32`
findings.replay_cell: independently upheld on fresh native and WASM outputs; exactly three metadata deltas

vet.evidence: Reproduced all 3 deltas on current main by source reading (hardcoded literals, decisive). Oracle: ghostty/src/terminal/c/types.zig:174-204 typeName() maps .enum→"enum"; ClipboardWrite.location is clipboard.Location=enum(c_int) (terminal/c/terminal.zig:80, clipboard.zig:2) → "enum". TerminalScrollbar=PageList.Scrollbar.C=extern struct{total,offset,len:u64} (PageList.zig:3359-3363) → 3 named u64 fields. ScrollViewport.C=extern struct{tag:Tag(enum),value:CValue(union)} (Terminal.zig:2519-2527, lib/union.zig:47-53) → fields tag:"enum"(off 0,sz 4)+value:"opaque"(off 8,sz 16). Rustty: crates/rustty-vt-c/src/types.rs:217 emits location as "i32"; types.rs:628-652 scrollbar_info/scrollviewport_info emit a single {value,offset 0,size=whole-struct,"opaque"} field for both. Yet Rustty's real C projections ARE field-bearing: ScrollbarC{total,offset,len:u64} (rustty-vt/src/pagelist/grow.rs:903-907), ScrollViewportC{tag:c_int,value:union[2]u64} (rustty-vt-c/src/terminal.rs:1877-1888). Internal inconsistency: same file emits "enum" for ProgressReport.state (types.rs:600). types.rs PORT NOTE 619-627 misstates both types as opaque "[N]u64 unions". git log: types.rs last touched 384d6299, predates audit pin dc054bb — not fixed since. DEFERRALS.md type_json mentions (5446,5502) concern WASM runtime proof only, not field maps.
vet.fix_plan: In crates/rustty-vt-c/src/types.rs: (1) line 217 change "i32"→"enum" for ClipboardWrite.location (matches oracle typeName of enum(c_int); ABI unchanged). (2) Replace scrollbar_info::<T>() with struct_info!(TerminalScrollbar, [("total",u64,total,"u64"),("offset",u64,offset,"u64"),("len",u64,len,"u64")]). (3) Replace scrollviewport_info::<T>() with struct_info!(ScrollViewportC, [("tag",c_int,tag,"enum"),("value",ScrollViewportCValue,value,"opaque")]) — type string "enum" because the oracle reflects Tag as enum; Rustty's D11 c_int field is ABI-identical, and resolve_ty passes "enum"/"opaque" through. offset_of! yields tag=0, value=8 matching Ghostty. (4) Rewrite the stale PORT NOTE at 619-627. Proving test: extend the existing types.rs #[test] json parse tests to assert scrollbar fields total/offset/len with type "u64", scrollviewport fields tag(type "enum",offset 0,size 4)/value(type "opaque",offset 8,size 16), and clip_write location type=="enum" (Ghostty has no per-type-string test; adding one is allowed). Run: cargo test -p rustty-vt-c types.
vet.severity_assessment: Agree P3: metadata-only reflection API divergence (sizes/aligns correct) but it actively misleads WASM/FFI binding generators about 3 public structs.
vet.notes: Report is accurate and complete: exactly three deltas, no more (ProgressReport.state correctly "enum"). Nuance the report understates: the types.rs PORT NOTE's own justification is factually wrong — ScrollbarC is a plain field-bearing repr(C) struct, not a union, so the "cannot reflect a union" rationale never applied to it; and ScrollViewportC has an addressable tag field the metadata omits entirely (consumers cannot locate the tag at offset 0 vs payload at offset 8). Ghostty value-union field is reported size 16 at offset 8, whereas Rustty reports one value field size 24 at offset 0 — offsets, not just type labels, diverge. W16-CABI-01 (lazy WASM allocation) is a distinct finding, not part of this group.

findings.title: kqueue timers armed after a blocking callback derive their deadline from stale cached time and can fire immediately
findings.replay_cell: independently upheld; FreeBSD impact latent behind W4-01

vet.evidence: Confirmed by close reading both sides on current main (d34cc15). Oracle: Ghostty pin's frozen libxev (build.zig.zon:19-22, hash 86vtcwIRFAD…, commit 9ce8e8e6) at zig-pkg/libxev-…/src/backend/kqueue.zig:664-688 has `timer_next(self: *Loop, …)` calling `self.update_now()` at :680 before adding the delay to cached_now, plus a regression test "kqueue: timer fired after loop is blocked" (~:2760-2861) asserting elapsed_ms >= timer_delay_ms after a delayed mach-port wake arms a timer from the callback. Rustty: crates/rustty-xev/src/kqueue.rs:1138-1168 `timer_next(&self, …)` adds the delay to `self.cached_now` (:1159, :1163) with NO update_now; the cache is refreshed only before the blocking kevent wait (:736, :1040-1046). So a timer armed from a callback reached after a blocking wait longer than the requested delay gets an already-past deadline and fires immediately. `git log dc054bb..HEAD -- crates/rustty-xev/` is empty (0 commits) — unchanged since the audit pin, whose red/green replay (fail 3x at ~20us; pass 5x after the 2-line mutation) I accept as consistent with this source trace. No ported regression test exists (no "blocked"-loop timer test in rustty-xev). Root cause of the miss: the port and its test-count gate (.port/tools/gates/check_test_counts.py:178, XEV_BLUEPRINT.md:4) pin the OLD libxev cache dir 86vtc4Ic…, not the manifest's 86vtcwIR…. No deferral doc mentions timer_next or the libxev pin skew.
vet.fix_plan: In /Users/gael/projects/rustty/crates/rustty-xev/src/kqueue.rs change `fn timer_next(&self, next_ms: u64)` (line 1138) to `&mut self` and insert `self.update_now();` after the next_s/next_ns overflow casts, immediately before building the deadline Timespec — exactly mirroring oracle kqueue.zig:680. All three call sites (timer :1067, timer_reset Adding :1102, timer_reset Active :1112) are already inside `&mut self` methods operating on raw `*mut Completion`, so the borrow change compiles without restructuring. Proving test: port the oracle regression test "kqueue: timer fired after loop is blocked and callback modifies the loop" into rustty-xev (an Async/machport watcher woken after ~50ms arms a 20ms timer from its callback; assert callback-to-fire elapsed >= 20ms and trigger == expiration) — the audit's retained probe wave13-kqueue-stale-timer.rs is a ready-made template that was shown red-before/green-after. Optionally (adjacent, W13A-02 scope) repoint .port/tools/gates/check_test_counts.py:178 at the manifest-pinned libxev tree so future upstream test additions are counted.
vet.severity_assessment: Agree with P3: real runtime divergence on the live macOS kqueue path, but bounded impact — one early timer fire per stale-arm, no crash/UB.
vet.notes: Single-member group; registry row INDEX.md:211 matches. Report is accurate; one framing correction: "Non-macOS impact: latent FreeBSD" undersells that kqueue IS the executing macOS backend, so this is a live primary-platform bug, not only latent. The gap exists because rustty-xev was ported from an older libxev snapshot (86vtc4Ic…) than the one Ghostty's pinned manifest freezes (86vtcwIR…); nothing in DEFERRALS.md/GAP_ANALYSIS.md/XEV_BLUEPRINT.md documents that skew as deliberate.

findings.replay_cell: independently upheld; default is off in both projects and no minidump execution is claimed

vet.evidence: Reproduced on current main d34cc15 (cited files unchanged since pin; last commits b8e4ae01/8aec487d). Rustty: crates/rustty-crash/src/build_options.rs:32 hardcodes SENTRY=cfg!(macos||ios); no cargo feature override exists in rustty-crash or sentry-sys Cargo.toml (grep: no [features]); sentry.rs:169-172 early-returns when false. crates-sys/sentry-sys/build.rs:101 unconditionally defines SENTRY_BACKEND_INPROC and :164 compiles only src/backends/sentry_backend_inproc.c; Cargo.toml header states breakpad/crashpad "NOT vendored"; no breakpad-sys crate. Oracle (ghostty 6ad1fe7d): src/build/Config.zig:181-194 -Dsentry is user-overridable on any target; src/build/SharedDeps.zig:407-431 passes .backend=.breakpad and links the breakpad archive whenever sentry is enabled; pkg/sentry/build.zig:42,164-181 defines SENTRY_BACKEND_BREAKPAD, compiles sentry_backend_breakpad.cpp, links breakpad; pkg/breakpad/build.zig builds both Linux and mac client sources. W15-04's Linux framing is correct but under-scoped; the backend mismatch is live on macOS today, not just behind an unavailable Linux toggle. findings.title: first `rustty_type_json()` call grows WASM memory and detaches existing JavaScript views
findings.replay_cell: independently upheld with bounded wasm probe; distinct from W12-05/F-006/F-008

vet.evidence: Reproduced myself on current main (d34cc15; `git diff dc054bb..HEAD -- crates/rustty-vt-c/ include/rustty/` is empty, so pin==main here). Source: crates/rustty-vt-c/src/types.rs:681-689 caches JSON in `static JSON: OnceLock<Vec<u8>>` built at first call by json_write_all() (types.rs:659-673); types.rs:702-704 returns its ptr; lib.rs:1524 exports rustty_type_json. Oracle: ghostty/src/terminal/c/types.zig:78-88 builds `pub const json: [:0]const u8` at comptime (zero runtime alloc); main.zig:217 exports it. I rebuilt rustty-vt-c for wasm32-unknown-unknown from current main into scratchpad (4.98s, exit 0) and re-ran the audit probe (.port/codex/line-audit/waves/probes/wave16-type-json-memory-growth-independent.mjs, node v25.6.0) against it + ghostty/zig-out/bin/ghostty-vt.wasm: rustty call 1 grew memory 1376256->1441792 (one 64KiB page), sameBuffer:false, priorViewBytes:0 (pre-existing Uint8Array detached); call 2 stable (cache control). Ghostty both calls: same buffer, no growth, prior views live. JSON parsed validly in all cases, so it is purely a first-call wasm memory-growth side effect. Header contract include/rustty/vt/types.h:300-333 and wasm.h:35-62 (identical to ghostty's) document reusable DataView over wasmMemory.buffer, which this violates. types.rs:24-32 PORT NOTE documents runtime-vs-comptime as deliberate but never mentions the wasm view-detachment hazard; no DEFERRALS.md/GAP_ANALYSIS.md row covers it.
vet.fix_plan: In crates/rustty-vt-c/src/types.rs, replace the OnceLock<Vec<u8>> runtime cache with true static data, mirroring the oracle's comptime two-pass (count, then fill): rewrite json_stringify/json_write_all as const fns emitting into a fixed [u8; MAX] buffer (offset_of!/size_of/align_of are all const-stable; integer formatting via a small const itoa), compute `const JSON_LEN`, then `static JSON_BYTES: [u8; JSON_LEN + 1]` with NUL sentinel; get_json() returns JSON_BYTES.as_ptr(). No lib.rs change (export signature unchanged). Behavioral delta vs oracle closes to zero: rustty_type_json becomes allocation-free static data like ghostty_type_json, so the first call cannot memory.grow or detach host views. Proof: (1) keep/extend the existing json_parses test plus a new test asserting the const-built bytes equal the current json_write_all() output (guards byte-identical formatting during the rewrite); (2) re-run the wave16 probe (probes/wave16-type-json-memory-growth-independent.mjs) with inverted rustty expectations — call 1 must show sameBuffer:true, beforeBytes==afterBytes, live prior view — ideally wired as a repeatable gate script. Fallback if const-eval of the full stringify proves too invasive: generate the static via a #[test]-checked include! golden; the OnceLock must go either way. Also note the ~160-byte jsonBytes delta (8108 vs 8268) is W12-05 content drift, tracked separately — do not fold it into this fix.
vet.severity_assessment: Agree with P3: real first-call view-detachment hazard for browser embedders, but metadata-only getter with a trivial host workaround (call once at startup, reacquire buffer).
vet.notes: Single-member group; the INDEX rows W17-B06/W91-B03/W91-B06 are duplicates upholding the same finding, not additional gaps. The report's dedupe against W12-05 (content deltas), F-006 (private callback table), and F-008 (allocator domain) is correct — I verified the probe exercises only the exported getter. The types.rs module doc comment (lines 1-6) still claims "embedded in the binary as a const string", which is currently false and should be corrected by the fix. WASM-target work is broadly questioned in GAP_ANALYSIS.md item 244(d), but rustty-vt-c's wasm C-ABI surface itself is ported and building, and this hazard has no deferral row, so known_deferred=false.

fix.detail: Replaced the OnceLock<Vec<u8>> runtime cache with true comptime static data, mirroring the oracle's two-pass build: StructInfo.fields is now &'static [FieldInfo], STRUCTS is a const, the stringify helpers are const fn over a byte buffer (str_eq added since str match isn't const), json_len() counts in a const-eval-local scratch, and `static JSON: [u8; JSON_LEN+1] = json_bytes()` carries the [:0] sentinel; get_json returns JSON.as_ptr(). Module doc/PORT NOTE corrected (it now really is const data) and the WASM view-detachment hazard documented. Proof: adapted wave16 probe (inverted rustty expectations) on a fresh wasm32 build -> call 1 sameBuffer:true, beforeBytes==afterBytes==1376256, prior view live, matching ghostty exactly (was: 64KiB memory.grow + detached views). JSON bytes unchanged by the rewrite (8257 native, same as before).

findings.title: `rustty_wasm.wasm` retains Atlas exports but omits Ghostty's DeferredFace/WebCanvas face/shaper exports
findings.replay_cell: independently upheld with fresh wasm export inspection; alternate Rustty-prefixed artifact is not ABI-compatible

vet.evidence: Reproduced on current main (crates unchanged since pin: only d34cc15 "untrack codex stuff" after dc054bb). Oracle ghostty@6ad1fe7d src/font/main.zig:33-40 retains 4 wasm groups: Atlas.Wasm + DeferredFace.Wasm + face.web_canvas.Wasm + shape.web_canvas.Wasm; unprefixed exports at DeferredFace.zig:427/453/460 (deferred_face_new/free/load), face/web_canvas.zig:494/513/521/532 (face_new/free/render_glyph/debug_canvas), shaper/web_canvas.zig:236/253/262 (shaper_new/free/test). Rustty crates/rustty-wasm/src/lib.rs:61-110 retains ONLY config_*+atlas_*; Cargo.toml:53 deps rustty-font only (no rustty-font-shaper); tests/artifact_shape.rs:152-168 asserts only config_*/atlas_*/memory. Substitutes are prefixed+resignatured in a SEPARATE artifact: rustty-font-shaper/src/face/web_canvas.rs:768-837 exports rustty_wc_face_* (render_glyph writes caller out_glyph, returns i32; face_new pts:f32 vs oracle u16), shaper is rustty_wc_shaper_shape not shaper_test. Counterweight I verified: the oracle surface is DEAD upstream — grep finds main_wasm.zig referenced nowhere in ghostty build.zig/src, and face/web_canvas.zig:557 calls wasm.toHostOwned, deleted by upstream 9dc2e5978, so face.web_canvas.Wasm cannot compile at pin; no shipped Ghostty artifact exposes these names. DEFERRALS.md:5567 claim "reference DeferredFace.zig carries no Wasm C-ABI" is FALSE (DeferredFace.zig:423-466).
vet.fix_plan: Add a Ghostty-ABI wasm export module to rustty-font-shaper (new mod, cfg(target_arch="wasm32") + feature "ghostty-wasm-abi"): unprefixed deferred_face_new/free/load, face_new/free/render_glyph/face_debug_canvas, shaper_new/free/shaper_test with oracle signatures (face_new pts:u16; face_render_glyph returns *mut Glyph allocated via the resurrected rustty_os::wasm tracker — rustty already ported toHostOwned that upstream deleted, so the faithful port compiles where the oracle does not; shaper_test mirrors shaper/web_canvas.zig:262 semantics). Wire retention: rustty-wasm/Cargo.toml gains rustty-font-shaper dep (legal — layering doctrine only forbids rustty-font→shaper edges, and rustty-web-canvas already links the shaper freestanding); add a #[used] retention tuple in rustty-wasm/src/lib.rs mod retain, mirroring the oracle's font/main.zig retention of all four groups. Proving test: extend crates/rustty-wasm/tests/artifact_shape.rs export-assert list with the 10 unprefixed names, and rebuild via .port/tools/build-main-wasm.sh --release (test is RED today — verified the names are absent from the current assert list). Also correct the false DEFERRALS.md:5567 "no Wasm C-ABI" claim.
vet.severity_assessment: Agree with P3 — real ABI-surface divergence, but the missing oracle exports are unbuilt, non-compiling dead code upstream, so no host can actually depend on them; fidelity-of-record only.
vet.notes: Not a documented deliberate deferral: DEFERRALS.md (rustty-font-shaper web_canvas section, ~5551-5575) documents the prefixed rustty_wc_* design in the separate rustty_web_canvas.wasm, but rests on the falsified premise that DeferredFace.zig has no Wasm C-ABI, and the WS14 record (DEFERRALS.md ~5518-5525, plan 2026-07-23-ws14-wasm-webgl.md) claims the retention set is "the reference's, corrected" while retaining only 1 of font/main.zig's 4 wasm groups — the omission was never ledgered as a divergence. Port doctrine itself (RESIDUAL #1 STALE note: "dead upstream is a reason to record the divergence, not a licence to skip the port") argues this should be either ported or explicitly ledgered. Correction to the report: it did not surface that upstream face/web_canvas.zig:557 fails to compile at pin (deleted toHostOwned) and that main_wasm.zig is referenced nowhere in ghostty's build — the "JS host written against Ghostty's contract" scenario is hypothetical. W17-B06 is a duplicate of this finding. Minimal alternative fix if the team prefers: ledger the divergence explicitly in DEFERRALS.md and fix the false 5567 claim (docs-only), since the oracle contract is dead; the code-fix plan above is the full-fidelity option.

fix.detail: All 10 unprefixed Ghostty-ABI exports (deferred_face_new/free/load, face_new/free/render_glyph/debug_canvas, shaper_new/free/test) now in rustty_wasm.wasm via new rustty-font-shaper feature ghostty-wasm-abi (ON only in rustty-wasm; rustty_web_canvas.wasm surface unchanged, verified). face_render_glyph returns host-owned *Glyph via resurrected to_host_owned, freed by exported free (runtime-proven in node). shaper_test's deleted *GroupCache modernized to *SharedGrid, terminal row-walk over modern rustty-vt per file precedent. Artifact stays freestanding (env-only imports, glue already covers them). DEFERRALS.md false claim (5567) corrected + WS14 retention overstatement ledgered.

findings.title: GTK terminal child environment does not use Ghostty's Flatpak empty-env baseline
findings.replay_cell: independently upheld; source-predicate replay, no live Flatpak session

vet.evidence: Oracle pin 6ad1fe7d (verified via git rev-parse in /Users/gael/projects/ghostty): src/apprt/gtk/class/surface.zig:1593-1599 `defaultTermioEnv` starts from `std.process.Environ.Map.init(alloc)` (empty) when `internal_os.isFlatpak()`, else `global.environMap()`. That branch was added by oracle commit b988efcfe (2026-07-22, "fix some 0.16 translation regressions"), which IS inside the pin. Rustty current main (d34cc15): crates/rustty-apprt/src/gtk/class/surface.rs:2347-2351 `default_termio_env` unconditionally does `let mut env = rustty_global::environ_map();` — no Flatpak branch; the PORTS comment (:2337-2345) defers only snap filtering, and its cited line ranges (e.g. LANG at ":1598-1602") match the PRE-b988efcfe oracle text, i.e. a pin-reconciliation miss, not a deliberate skip. Detector exists and is always compiled: crates/rustty-os/src/flatpak.rs:28-41 `isFlatpak()` (rustty-apprt already deps rustty-os, Cargo.toml:121). Empty baseline is trivially constructible: `EnvMap = HashMap<Vec<u8>,Vec<u8>>` (crates/rustty-global/src/environ.rs:72), Default. No deferral entry for this baseline in .port/phase-2/DEFERRALS.md (flatpak entries there are WS20 termio FlatpakHostCommand, which LANDED — flatpak is not wholesale deferred); GAP_ANALYSIS.md workstream-6 flatpak rows don't name this method.
vet.fix_plan: In crates/rustty-apprt/src/gtk/class/surface.rs default_termio_env (:2347-2351), replace the unconditional `rustty_global::environ_map()` with the oracle branch: `let mut env = if rustty_os::flatpak::isFlatpak() { rustty_global::EnvMap::default() } else { rustty_global::environ_map() };` and update the PORTS comment to cite the pinned oracle lines (surface.zig:1593-1599, b988efcfe). Behavioral delta: under Flatpak, the child env starts EMPTY (then gains LANG/winproto/quick-terminal keys) instead of cloning the sandbox process env. Proving test: extract the baseline choice into a small helper `fn termio_env_baseline(is_flatpak: bool) -> EnvMap` used by default_termio_env, plus a unit test asserting flatpak=true yields an empty map and flatpak=false yields environ_map(); test lives with the GTK module and runs in the existing Linux/GTK lane (same lane as tests/gtk_x11_* KATs). Ghostty has no test for this; adding one is allowed.
vet.severity_assessment: Agree with P3: Flatpak-Linux-only behavior, but it leaks the full sandbox env to every child shell vs Ghostty's empty baseline.
vet.notes: Report is accurate, including its reachability chain (verified rt_surface.default_termio_env -> termio exact-env at rustty-core/src/surface.rs and rustty-termio/src/command.rs). One nuance the report missed: the in-file PORT NOTE's oracle line citations correspond to the pre-b988efcfe file, showing the method was ported from a pre-pin snapshot and never reconciled when the pin advanced past the 0.16-regressions fix — useful when auditing sibling methods in the same file for the same class of staleness. Distinct from F-011 (saved LANG), as the report says.

findings.title: GTK Flatpak resources-dir override is ported but unreachable from Rustty global init
findings.replay_cell: independently upheld; source-predicate replay, no live Flatpak session

vet.deferral_ref: .port/phase-2/GAP_ANALYSIS.md workstream 7 "linux-gtk-frontend" (GTK apprt subsystem sequenced last; depends on workstream 6 "platform-linux-windows ... flatpak") — the enclosing GTK-runtime wiring is a documented deferral, though this exact resources-dir routing row is not itemized. Also crates/rustty-apprt/src/lib.rs:26-33 PORT NOTE documents that Ghostty's comptime runtime switch is replaced by consumer/cfg selection, with the gtk backend cfg-gated and its bin binding deferred to L5.5.
vet.evidence: Verified on rustty main d34cc154 vs ghostty 6ad1fe7d. Oracle: src/apprt/gtk.zig:4 exports `resourcesDir = @import("gtk/flatpak.zig").resourcesDir`; src/global.zig:213-214 calls `apprt.runtime.resourcesDir(self.alloc)` (comptime-dispatched: gtk artifact gets the Flatpak-aware helper, src/apprt/gtk/flatpak.zig:7-29; none/embedded alias internal_os.resourcesDir). Rustty: crates/rustty-apprt/src/gtk/flatpak.rs:20-69 is a faithful port of the helper, but grep across crates/ finds NO production caller of `gtk::flatpak::resources_dir` — only its own parity test (flatpak.rs:89). Global init at crates/rustty-apprt/src/lib.rs:330-331 keeps the oracle comment yet hardcodes `rustty_os::resourcesDir()`; gtk.rs:93-110 only declares `pub mod flatpak;` (no runtime re-export), and the gtk module itself is `#[cfg(all(target_os="linux", feature="gtk"))]` (lib.rs:47-48). So under a GTK build the Flatpak override is unreachable — report reproduced. Dormancy also reconfirmed: rustty-build-config build.rs:113 sets `flatpak: false` const, lib.rs:213-214 exposes it, and flatpak.rs:24 gates on it, so the Flatpak arm is dead code in every current build regardless of routing. Hardcoded rustty_os::resourcesDir() equals Ghostty's embedded/none runtime behavior, so the macOS-first artifact is faithful today.
vet.severity_assessment: Agree with P3: latent unreachability only — no supported build diverges today (gtk cfg-gated to Linux, flatpak const-false), but it will silently misroute once the GTK/Flatpak tier goes live.
vet.notes: Eventual fix is surgical and plan-consistent: add `pub use flatpak::resources_dir;` as the gtk runtime hook in gtk.rs and a cfg-gated arm in lib.rs init (`#[cfg(all(target_os="linux", feature="gtk"))]` call gtk::flatpak::resources_dir(), else rustty_os::resourcesDir()), mirroring the documented cfg-as-comptime-switch selector. Classified deferred-platform because it cannot be compiled or proven on this macOS host (gtk4-rs deps are Linux-target-gated) and the init-time runtime binding belongs to the deferred L5.5 GTK bin work. One report correction: it cites build.rs:111-113 as a "caveat", but note WS20 (DEFERRALS.md:913-943) moved the REAL -Dflatpak toggle to rustty-termio/rustty-os cargo features, while gtk/flatpak.rs:24 (and exec.rs:1963) still gate on the const-false rustty_build_config::flatpak() — a second latent inconsistency in how the flatpak flag is plumbed, worth folding into the same future fix. Single-member group; member row == group finding.

fix.detail: Read the oracle first: apprt/gtk.zig:4 `pub const resourcesDir = @import("gtk/flatpak.zig").resourcesDir;` is the third member of the required comptime apprt API (none.zig:6 / browser.zig:2 / embedded.zig:28 alias internal_os.resourcesDir instead), consumed at exactly one site, global.zig:214 `self.resources_dir = try apprt.runtime.resourcesDir(self.alloc)`. findings.title: vxfw `App.deinit` skips `Tty::deinit()` on normal shutdown/error, unlike libvaxis 0.5.1
findings.replay_cell: independently upheld; reachable through `rustty +boo`, distinct from panic recovery

vet.evidence: Reproduced on main d34cc154. crates/rustty-vaxis/src/vxfw/app.rs:82-88: `pub fn deinit(&mut self)` calls only `self.vx.deinit(writer)`; comment claims "tty.deinit() ... performed by the caller dropping self" but no `impl Drop` exists for PosixTty/Tty/App (only VxfwArena has Drop in the crate, vxfw/mod.rs:841), so dropping frees memory without restoring termios. tty.rs:283-292: `PosixTty::deinit(self)` is consuming — tcsetattr(TCSAFLUSH) restore + close(fd) on non-macOS; never invoked on the +boo path. boo.rs:455,477,481: `App::init` → `app.run` → `app.deinit()` — reachable via `rustty +boo`. Oracle libvaxis 0.5.1 (the documented rustty-vaxis pin) App.zig:48-52 calls BOTH `self.vx.deinit(...)` and `self.tty.deinit()`; tty.zig:86-92 matches Rustty's deinit body. Vaxis::deinit (vaxis.rs reset_state) emits reset escape sequences only — it cannot undo termios raw mode, so the terminal is left raw after +boo exits, on macOS too (only close(fd) is macOS-skipped, not tcsetattr). Sibling CLI paths do it right: list_themes.rs:828-830, list_keybinds, list_colors all call `vx.deinit(); tty.deinit()`, proving the omission is localized to vxfw App. Not a documented deferral: DEFERRALS.md:2970-2994 deferred boo, but e7e5a8c1 un-deferred it; no doc defers Tty cleanup. Distinct from W16-EXPLICIT-01 (panic-hook recovery).
vet.fix_plan: In crates/rustty-vaxis/src/vxfw/app.rs change `pub fn deinit(&mut self)` to consuming `pub fn deinit(mut self)`: `let writer = self.tty.writer(); self.vx.deinit(writer); self.tty.deinit();` (App has no Drop impl, so moving the tty field out is legal; matches oracle App.zig:48-52 order vx-then-tty). Caller crates/rustty-cli/src/boo.rs:481 `app.deinit()` compiles unchanged (moves app; app is not used after). Behavioral delta: after `rustty +boo`, saved termios is restored via tcsetattr(TCSAFLUSH) and /dev/tty fd closed on non-macOS — identical to libvaxis 0.5.1. Proving test: under cfg(test) Tty=TestTty (tty.rs:82, TestTty::deinit at :911); give TestTty a deinit-observed flag (e.g. shared Arc<AtomicBool> or a static test counter) and add a rustty-vaxis test constructing App, calling deinit(), asserting the tty deinit ran; optionally extend crates/rustty-cli/tests/boo_pty_e2e.rs to tcgetattr the pty slave after child exit and assert ICANON/ECHO restored.
vet.severity_assessment: Agree P3 at minimum; arguably P2 since every `rustty +boo` run on macOS (primary platform) leaves the terminal in raw mode until the shell resets it, plus an fd leak on other POSIX.
vet.notes: Single-member group; the in-source comment at app.rs:86-87 is actively wrong ("Rust frees the tty on drop — the reset already happened via vx.deinit"): vx.deinit resets escape-sequence state only, never termios. Report's citations all check out against current main; nothing stale.

findings.title: C `default_cursor_style` option accepts the public cursor-style sentinel instead of Ghostty's clean `invalid_value` path for unknown enum values
findings.replay_cell: independently upheld with linked C probe; not a duplicate

vet.evidence: Verified on current main (only commit since audit pin dc054bb is d34cc154 "untrack codex stuff"; git log shows no change to crates/rustty-vt-c/src/terminal.rs). Oracle: ghostty/src/terminal/c/terminal.zig:706-708 `default_cursor_style` does `toZig() orelse return .invalid_value`; TerminalCursorStyle is non-exhaustive `enum(c_int){bar=0..block_hollow=3, _}` with `_ => null` (:725-740), so any unknown c_int returns INVALID_VALUE. Rustty: crates/rustty-vt-c/src/terminal.rs:1714-1733 reads `value as *const TerminalCursorStyle` and derefs `unsafe { *ptr }` where TerminalCursorStyle is a CLOSED #[repr(C)] enum with only variants 0..3 (:1789-1796); to_zig (:1813-1824) is exhaustive over the 4 variants with no None-returning unknown arm, so the `None => Result::InvalidValue` at :1724 is structurally unreachable. Reachable from public ABI: include/rustty/vt/terminal.h:299 exposes RUSTTY_TERMINAL_CURSOR_STYLE_MAX_VALUE = RUSTTY_ENUM_MAX_VALUE = INT_MAX (types.h:69). Deref of an out-of-range discriminant into a closed Rust enum is UB; audit's linked C probe observed sentinel accepted with RUSTTY_SUCCESS. Port note at :1808-1812 claims the value is "rejected at the *ptr read" — incorrect (UB, not rejection). Not in .port/phase-2/DEFERRALS.md (only an unrelated resolved cursor-style row at :108). Crate already validates raw ints elsewhere (CompressionMode const-asserts ~:847; Result::InvalidValue on `_` at :1156).
vet.fix_plan: In crates/rustty-vt-c/src/terminal.rs, change the DefaultCursorStyle arm (:1714-1733) to read `value as *const c_int`, deref the raw int, and map it via a new `fn terminal_cursor_style_from_int(v: c_int) -> Option<rustty_vt::screen::CursorStyle>` matching 0..=3 to Bar/Block/Underline/BlockHollow and `_ => None` (mirroring the oracle's non-exhaustive `_ => null`); null ptr still defaults to Block; None returns Result::InvalidValue. This removes the UB deref and makes the InvalidValue arm reachable, matching Ghostty exactly. Rewrite the incorrect port note at :1808-1812. Proving test: add a unit test near set_default_cursor_style_and_blink (:4180) that calls rustty_terminal_set with OPT_DEFAULT_CURSOR_STYLE pointing at c_int values 2147483647 (the header sentinel) and 4, asserting Result::InvalidValue and that the terminal's default cursor style is unchanged; keep a valid-value control asserting Success. Run: cargo test -p rustty-vt-c set_default_cursor_style.
vet.severity_assessment: Agree P3 as behavioral parity impact, but note the Rustty side is UB (invalid enum discriminant deref), which makes fixing it more than cosmetic.
vet.notes: Single-member group; the independent replay's probe output (sentinel_result=0/success instead of -2) is consistent with my source proof, and I did not need to rebuild the dylib to confirm — the closed enum plus exhaustive match makes the divergence structural. The report's claim that "unknown values are rejected at the pointer read" (echoing the in-code port note) is wrong in both places: nothing rejects the value; the read is UB and observed behavior is acceptance.

fix.detail: terminal.rs DefaultCursorStyle arm now reads *const c_int (not *const TerminalCursorStyle) and narrows via a new TerminalCursorStyle::from_c_int(c_int)->Option<Self> (0..=3, `_ => None`, mirroring the oracle's non-exhaustive `_ => null`); null ptr still defaults to Block; unknown values return Result::InvalidValue. This removes the invalid-discriminant deref UB and makes the InvalidValue arm reachable. Naming follows the crate's existing ScrollViewportTag::from_c_int precedent. The incorrect port note ("rejected at the *ptr read") was rewritten on both to_zig and the call site. Proving test confirmed decisive: with the call site temporarily reverted it FAILS (left: InvalidValue, right: Success) and passes with the fix.

findings.title: terminfo generation contradicts FreeBSD layout and hardcodes Unix tools
findings.replay_cell: upheld with correction

vet.evidence: Reproduced on main @ d34cc154 (file unchanged since audit pin dc054bb on these points). Generator: xtask/src/res_terminfo.rs:97 always joins "terminfo" under share/ (grep: zero "site-terminfo" hits in all of xtask/src); :136 hardcodes Command::new("/usr/bin/tic"); :170 hardcodes "/usr/bin/infotocap"; no Windows or FreeBSD branch anywhere in the file.
