findings.title: RGB parser edge cases diverge: Ghostty accepts NaN `rgbi` intensities as black while Rustty rejects them, and Rustty accepts signed hex components that Ghostty rejects
findings.replay_cell: independently upheld with correction that Rustty signed-hex acceptance is bounded by the component-length gate

vet.evidence: Read both parsers on current main (clean @ d34cc15). Rustty crates/rustty-vt/src/color.rs:907-914 from_intensity uses `(0.0..=1.0).contains(&i)` — NaN fails contains → Err. Ghostty src/terminal/color.zig:593-604 uses `if (i < 0.0 or i > 1.0)` — NaN fails both comparisons → passes; @intFromFloat(NaN*255)=0. Rustty color.rs:925 uses u16::from_str_radix (accepts leading '+'); Ghostty color.zig:616 std.fmt.parseUnsigned (rejects signs). Ran isolated probes replicating each helper verbatim (scratchpad rgbprobe.rs/rgbprobe.zig, zig 0.16 Debug+ReleaseFast): Rust: NaN/nan→Err, "+f"→Ok(15), "+0"→Ok(0), "+ffff"→Err(len gate), "-f"→Err. Zig: NaN/nan→ok(0) both modes, "+f"/"+ff"/"+0"→err. Matches audit's Ghostty product probe (.port/codex/evidence/w21-b04-color-tests-independent/ghostty-probe-output.txt: rgbi:NaN/0/0=ok(00,00,00), rgb:+f/0/0=err). Reachability confirmed: RGB::parse called from rustty-vt-c/src/color.rs:190, rustty-config/src/value_types.rs:2052, parse_palette_entry color.rs:126. No deferral covers this (grepped DEFERRALS.md/MAIN_PARITY.md/GAP_ANALYSIS.md for rgbi/RGB parse edges — none). NEW extra divergence found: Zig parseUnsigned accepts interior '_' separators ("f_f"→ok(255), so Ghostty accepts "rgb:f_f/0/0"→15) while Rust from_str_radix rejects — same helper, unreported.
vet.fix_plan: In /Users/gael/projects/rustty/crates/rustty-vt/src/color.rs: (1) from_intensity (line 909): replace `if !(0.0..=1.0).contains(&i)` with `if i < 0.0 || i > 1.0` (Zig comparison semantics: NaN passes); Rust `as u8` cast then maps NaN→0 = black, exactly matching observed Ghostty output; inf stays rejected (inf>1.0). (2) from_hex (line 925): replace bare u16::from_str_radix with a std.fmt.parseUnsigned-faithful parse: reject leading '+'/'-'; allow interior '_' digit separators but not leading/trailing (strip '_' after validating positions, then from_str_radix); keep the length gate and divisor keyed on the RAW value.len() including underscores, as Zig does. Proving test: extend #[test] rgb_parse in the same file: RGB::parse("rgbi:NaN/0/0")==Ok(RGB{0,0,0}), "rgbi:nan/0/0"==Ok(RGB{0,0,0}), "rgb:+f/0/0"==Err, "rgb:+0/0/0"==Err, "rgb:f_f/0/0"==Ok(RGB{r:15,g:0,b:0}), "rgbi:inf/0/0"==Err. Run: cargo test -p rustty-vt rgb_parse.
vet.severity_assessment: Agree P3: obscure edge inputs, no crash, but reaches config/C-API/OSC/kitty color paths.
vet.notes: Report correction upheld: signed-hex acceptance is bounded by the 4-char component-length gate ("+ffff" rejected), and "+f" yields 15 (len-2 divisor), not 255. "-f" is rejected by both (unsigned overflow). Note Ghostty's NaN path is technically @intFromFloat safety-checked-illegal territory in Zig, but observed behavior is ok(0) in both Debug and ReleaseFast on zig 0.16 arm64, and the port fix (Rust saturating cast) reproduces it safely. Additional unreported member of the same gap: underscore digit separators in hex components (Ghostty accepts "f_f", Rustty rejects) — recommend folding into the same fix.

findings.title: Rustty `AutoContext` uses Rust `DefaultHasher` rather than Ghostty seed-0 Wyhash, preserving logical lookups but changing physical hash-map slots, fingerprints, iterator order, and reachable raw page backing bytes consumed by compression
findings.replay_cell: independently upheld with narrowing: raw compression input/encoded-byte divergence is directly proven; retain/discard threshold flip remains plausible but unproven

vet.evidence: Reproduced on current main (d34cc15; `git log dc054bb..HEAD -- crates/rustty-vt/src/hash_map.rs` is empty, file unchanged since audit pin). Rustty crates/rustty-vt/src/hash_map.rs:143-149: AutoContext::hash builds std::collections::hash_map::DefaultHasher (zero-keyed SipHash-1-3). Ghostty (verified pin 6ad1fe7d via git rev-parse) src/terminal/hash_map.zig:71-90: seed-0 Wyhash over asBytes(&key) (force-inlined for unique-representation keys). Different algorithms give different u64s for essentially all keys; slot derives from low bits (hash_map.rs:573-574 `hash & mask`) and metadata fingerprint from top 7 bits (hash_map.rs:664 take_fingerprint), matching Ghostty's derivation (hash_map.zig:462-472,556-563) — so physical slots/fingerprints/iterator order diverge exactly as reported. Reachable byte consumer confirmed: crates/rustty-vt/src/compress/page.rs:113-137 lz4-compresses the entire raw mapping (memory_ptr..memory_len), which contains the map key/value/metadata slots, so logically equal pages produce different encoded bytes/ratios vs the oracle. The substitution is a documented deliberate choice in-source: PORT NOTE hash_map.rs:112-119 ("any deterministic hash suffices for the behavioral tests"); MAIN_PARITY.md:262-266 records porting only the #[inline] half of f2a7652ab. No shared consumer serializes iteration order (report's consumer search spot-checked: page maps used only via keyed get/update/remove).

Expose one-shot `hash(seed, &[u8])` plus a streaming struct implementing core::hash::Hasher whose write_uN methods update with to_ne_bytes, reproducing Zig autoHash/asBytes for the scoped keys (Offset<T> = u32, integers). Behavioral delta: AutoContext::hash (hash_map.rs:143-149) switches from DefaultHasher to Wyhash seed 0, making home slots, fingerprints, iterator order, and raw page backing bytes match the oracle. Proving tests: (1) rustty-zigstd golden-vector test using the seed-0 rows of Zig std wyhash.zig's smhasher test table; (2) hash_map.rs test inserting keys 0,1,2,3,4,8,16,24 (values 1000+k) at capacity 8 and asserting iterator order equals the Ghostty probe order [(16,1016),(24,1024),(4,1004),(8,1008),(1,1001),(0,1000),(2,1002),(3,1003)] recorded in wave-24-b01-hash-map-front-primary.md. vet.severity_assessment: Agree with P3: logical lookups intact; observable drift limited to compressed-page bytes/ratios and possible retain/discard threshold flips vs oracle, not correctness.
vet.notes: Report is accurate and its narrowing is honest: the retain/discard threshold-flip claim remains plausible-unproven (I did not attempt to prove it either). Nuances: (a) DefaultHasher::new() is fixed-key, so Rustty is deterministic and self-consistent — the gap is cross-implementation fidelity only; pages are never exchanged between Ghostty and Rustty processes, so no interop breakage. (b) The divergence is a documented deliberate in-source substitution (PORT NOTE hash_map.rs:112-119), but it is NOT a macOS-first plan deferral and appears in none of DEFERRALS.md/MAIN_PARITY.md/GAP_ANALYSIS.md as a deferral row, hence known_deferred=false. (c) Sibling occurrence of the same pattern at crates/rustty-vt/src/hyperlink.rs:331 (Wyhash replaced for hyperlink hashing) should be audited/fixed alongside, but is outside this finding group. (d) Fixing will change Rustty's own physical layouts, so any tests asserting current iteration order or compressed sizes may need regolding.

findings.title: Rustty `print_string` maps invalid UTF-8 validation failure to `OutOfMemory`, while Ghostty propagates the Unicode validator error (`InvalidUtf8`)
findings.replay_cell: independently upheld

vet.evidence: Reproduced on current main d34cc15 (cited files unchanged since audit pin dc054bb; git log dc054bb..HEAD over terminal.rs/screen.rs is empty). Rustty crates/rustty-vt/src/terminal.rs:1150-1157: `print_string` returns `Result<(), OutOfMemory>` and does `core::str::from_utf8(str).map_err(|_| OutOfMemory)?` — invalid UTF-8 is reported as OutOfMemory. Oracle ghostty/src/terminal/Terminal.zig:473-474: `printString` does `try std.unicode.Utf8View.init(str)`, whose inferred error set propagates error.InvalidUtf8, distinct from Allocator.Error/OutOfMemory. Member W29-B02-001's second site also confirmed: crates/rustty-vt/src/screen.rs:4961-4968 `Screen::test_write_string` has the identical `map_err(|_| OutOfMemory)` vs Ghostty Screen.zig testWriteString's `try Utf8View.init`. Both Rust sites carry PORT NOTEs acknowledging Utf8View validation yet still collapse the error class. No deferral: grep for InvalidUtf8/invalid-utf across DEFERRALS.md, MAIN_PARITY.md, INTEGRATION_PARITY.md, GAP_ANALYSIS.md returned nothing. Impact is bounded: Ghostty prod callers discard the error (termio/Thread.zig:181,199,219 `catch {}`; Surface.zig:1298 `catch break`), and Rustty mirrors that (rustty-termio/src/thread.rs:400 `let _ =`; rustty-core/src/surface.rs:3755ff), so the divergence is error classification, not runtime behavior.
vet.fix_plan: Add a two-variant error enum (e.g. `PrintStringError { OutOfMemory, InvalidUtf8 }` with `impl From<OutOfMemory>`) next to the existing `pagelist::OutOfMemory` use in rustty-vt. Change `Terminal::print_string` (terminal.rs:1150) and `Screen::test_write_string` (screen.rs:4961) to return `Result<(), PrintStringError>`, mapping `str::from_utf8` failure to `InvalidUtf8` and internal print/linefeed OutOfMemory via `?`+From. Behavioral delta vs oracle: invalid UTF-8 now yields a distinct InvalidUtf8 error exactly as Zig's `try Utf8View.init` propagates error.InvalidUtf8, while allocation failures keep OutOfMemory. Callers: rustty-termio/src/thread.rs:400 already discards; rustty-core/src/surface.rs:3755-3960 uses `?`/if-err — map with `.map_err(...)` or extend that fn's error; test `.unwrap()` sites compile unchanged. Proving test (rustty-vt): `t.print_string(b"foo\xFFbar")` returns `Err(PrintStringError::InvalidUtf8)` and screen unchanged; same for `Screen::test_write_string`; plus a valid-input regression case (Ghostty has no such test — additive is allowed).
vet.severity_assessment: Agree with P3: real classification divergence, but all production callers in both trees discard or merely propagate the error, so no user-visible behavior change.
vet.notes: Registry rows W29-B02 and W29-B02-001 are consistent; W29-B02-001 is the canonical dedupe row that also covers Screen::test_write_string (added by W43-B02 replay) — verified both sites independently. Report is accurate; its probe result (Err(OutOfMemory) vs zig InvalidUtf8) matches close reading of current sources. One nuance the report understates: the PORT NOTEs at both sites show the porter knew Utf8View validates, so this was a conscious but undocumented narrowing, not an oversight in reading the oracle — still a gap since it is recorded in no deferral doc.

fix.detail: Added pub enum PrintStringError{OutOfMemory,InvalidUtf8} with From<OutOfMemory> in rustty-vt terminal.rs (next to ResizeError, matching its idiom). Terminal::print_string and Screen::test_write_string now return Result<(),PrintStringError>, mapping str::from_utf8 failure to InvalidUtf8 (Zig error.InvalidUtf8 from try Utf8View.init) while allocation errors keep OutOfMemory via ?+From. Propagated through rustty-core surface.rs childExitedAbnormally (closure + fn error type now PrintStringError, mirroring the Zig inferred !void error set); thread.rs let _ site and all .unwrap() test sites unchanged. Both stale PORT NOTEs updated; no ledger rows existed for this gap. Note: mid-run a parallel agent briefly broke rustty-os/xdg.rs (dependency) — polled until green, unrelated to this fix.

findings.title: Terminal scalar print/cursor normal behavior matched, but independent replay found an extra Rustty allocation during cross-page wide-grapheme transfer
findings.replay_cell: independent replay corrected primary

vet.evidence: Reproduced on current main (d34cc15; terminal.rs unchanged since audit pin dc054bb — `git log dc054bb..HEAD -- crates/rustty-vt/src/terminal.rs` is empty). Rustty crates/rustty-vt/src/terminal.rs:2103-2114 (cross-page arm of the `'transfer_graphemes` block, entered only when new_pin.node != old_pin.node): `let cps: Vec<u21> = cps.to_vec();` with a PORT NOTE (2106-2108) citing borrow aliasing, then the append_grapheme loop. Ghostty oracle src/terminal/Terminal.zig:1258-1262 iterates `lookupGrapheme(old_rac.cell).?` directly — no copy. Divergence is real: (1) one extra heap allocation per cross-page wide-grapheme transfer; (2) failure of that allocation aborts (Vec's handle_alloc_error) instead of propagating as Terminal::print OutOfMemory, whereas the append_grapheme calls are correctly mapped via `.map_err(|_| OutOfMemory)?`. The copy is provably unnecessary under the same invariant Zig relies on: screen.rs:3636-3710 shows Screen::append_grapheme mutates/grows ONLY the cursor's page node (increase_capacity on `(*self.cursor.page_pin).node`), and this branch guarantees old_pin.node is a different node, so old-page grapheme memory (a separate page allocation, not behind &mut Screen) stays valid across the loop. Not documented as a deferral: no entry in .port/phase-2/DEFERRALS.md, ALLOC_AUDIT.md, or parity docs (PERF_LOG.md:202's cps.to_vec is a different site, the cell-clone path). No existing test covers this transfer path (grep terminal.rs tests).
vet.fix_plan: File: crates/rustty-vt/src/terminal.rs:2100-2117. Replace the `cps.to_vec()` copy with raw ptr+len iteration per the project's raw-ptr doctrine: capture `let (ptr, len) = (cps.as_ptr(), cps.len());` (provenance through the `old_page` raw pointer), drop the slice binding, then `for i in 0..len { let cp = unsafe { *ptr.add(i) }; self.active_mut().append_grapheme(new_rac.cell, cp).map_err(|_| OutOfMemory)?; }`. Behavioral delta vs oracle: eliminates the Rust-only allocation so the cross-page transfer path has exactly Ghostty's fallible-allocation set (only append_grapheme can fail, propagating as OutOfMemory; no abort-on-OOM site). Sound because this branch requires old_pin.node != new_pin.node and Screen::append_grapheme only mutates/reallocates the cursor's node (screen.rs:3653-3710) — the same invariant Zig's direct slice iteration relies on. Proving tests: (a) add a terminal test that fills to a page boundary and prints a wide char with attached grapheme (e.g. VS16 or ZWJ cluster) at right_limit-1 so the wrap crosses the page seam, asserting the cluster's codepoints moved to the new page cell and cleared from the old (Ghostty has no test for this block; additions allowed); (b) run that test under the vt Miri lane (or an isolated harness per shaper-hook-sb-clean-interleave) to prove the raw-ptr interleave is SB-clean — do not hand-reason it; (c) existing lanes `cargo test -p rustty-vt terminal_vs16 / terminal_zero_width / grapheme` stay green.
vet.severity_assessment: Agree with P3: rare path (wide+grapheme wrap crossing a page seam), success-path behavior identical; only an extra alloc plus abort-vs-OutOfMemory on alloc failure.
vet.notes: Registry row W29-B03 ("P3 corrected") and member W29-B03-001 accurately describe the finding; the primary batch's behavioral claims (print/cursor parity) were corroborated by the independent replay's 26 passing focused tests. One correction to the report's framing: the to_vec is not needed for soundness at all — the report says it "cannot be mapped to OutOfMemory", but the cleaner remedy is removing the allocation entirely (raw ptr+len), which the port's own doctrine (shaper-hook-sb-clean-interleave, rust-mut-args-strongly-protected memories) already prescribes for exactly this interleave shape. The in-code PORT NOTE documents intent but no deferral doc admits the divergence, so known_deferred=false.

fix.detail: Removed the Rust-only `cps.to_vec()` in print's cross-page `transfer_graphemes` arm (terminal.rs ~2124); now iterates the old page's grapheme slice by raw ptr+len, exactly as Terminal.zig:1258-1262 does in place. Kills the extra alloc and its abort-on-OOM; only append_grapheme can now fail (mapped to OutOfMemory). Miri: UB=0 on the new seam test.

vet.evidence: Reproduced by close reading on current main (d34cc15; only .port untracking since audit pin dc054bb, code identical). But grapheme tails bypass Cell storage: page_impl.rs:2231-2236 `set_graphemes(&mut self, row, cell, cps: &[u32])` -> :2264 `slice.copy_from_slice(cps)` (verbatim arena store, no mask/assert); :2288-2293 `append_grapheme(..., cp: u32)` -> :2320 `cps[0] = cp` (unchecked); :2382 `lookup_grapheme(&self, cell) -> Option<&[u32]>` returns the stored slice unchanged. Oracle ghostty/src/terminal/page.zig:1506 `setGraphemes(..., cps: []const u21)`, :1545 `appendGrapheme(..., cp: u21)`, :1607 `lookupGrapheme -> ?[]u21` — Zig's u21 type makes such a value a compile error (comptime) or safe-build @intCast panic; it cannot cross the API. No mention of u21 in DEFERRALS.md/MAIN_PARITY.md/INTEGRATION_PARITY.md/GAP_ANALYSIS.md (grep empty); the alias PORT NOTE is a documented design decision but its masking rationale does not cover the grapheme-tail arena path, and it is not a macOS-first platform deferral.

In crates/rustty-vt/src/page_impl.rs: in set_graphemes_inner (near line 2249) add `debug_assert!(cps.iter().all(|&cp| cp <= 0x1F_FFFF))`; in append_grapheme_inner (near line 2306, alongside the existing cfg(debug_assertions) codepoint!=0 assert) add `debug_assert!(cp <= 0x1F_FFFF)`. Update the PORT NOTE at page.rs:67-71 to state grapheme tails are debug-asserted, not masked. Ghostty has no equivalent test (enforced by the type system); adding tests is allowed.

findings.title: Non-UTF-8 POSIX `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` is discarded before Rustty default config-file discovery because the XDG helper converts non-empty env bytes through UTF-8, while Ghostty keeps the raw byte slice and joins it into the config path
findings.replay_cell: independently found by B02 and upheld by targeted B06 replay; Rustty probes fell back to `$HOME/.config/rustty/...`, while Ghostty `os/xdg.zig` uses non-empty raw env bytes

(2) shared_grid_set.rs:305 comment claims "`c` drops on any `?` error" but Collection has no Drop — oracle SharedGridSet.zig:175 errdefer c.deinit. (3) codepoint_resolver.rs:331-335 comment claims drop releases face — true for CoreText, false for Fontconfig; oracle CodepointResolver.zig:198,212 calls deferred_face.deinit(). (4) codepoint_resolver.rs:413,436 `?` bypasses disco_it.deinit() at :419/:439 — oracle :258 defer. (5) list_fonts.rs: `?` at :268-361 bypasses deinits :363-365 — oracle list_fonts.zig:108-118 defers. Nothing in DEFERRALS.md covers this.
vet.fix_plan: Reinstate the oracle's defer/errdefer semantics at each site, no API change: (1) collection.rs get_face_from_entry — on set_size error, call face.deinit() before returning Err (mirrors Collection.zig:232 errdefer); same in add()'s SetSizeFailed arm and add_deferred's early-error arms, deinit the moved face/DeferredFace before Err (net-equivalent to Ghostty's caller-side deferred_face.deinit() at CodepointResolver.zig:198/212). (2) shared_grid_set.rs collection() — wrap the body in an inner fn/closure returning Result and call c.deinit() on Err before propagating (SharedGridSet.zig:175 errdefer). (3) codepoint_resolver.rs get_index_codepoint_override — restructure the two `?` exits (:413, :436) so disco_it.deinit() runs on the error paths (CodepointResolver.zig:258 defer). (4) list_fonts.rs — move the fallible body into an inner fn; run disco_it/disco/font_lib deinit unconditionally afterward (list_fonts.zig defers). Fix the stale "drops on error" comments at collection.rs:324, shared_grid_set.rs:305, codepoint_resolver.rs:332-334. Proving test: rustty-font-shaper unit test with a cfg(test) deinit-counter (static AtomicUsize bumped in Face::deinit/DeferredFace::deinit) asserting deinit fires when add()/get_face_from_entry returns Err (force CollectionFull via SPECIAL_START-1 entries, force SetSizeFailed via a face whose set_size errors), and that Collection error-exit in shared_grid_set cleans owned entries.
vet.severity_assessment: Agree with P3: real cumulative native leaks (Fontconfig pattern, FT face, hb_font, boxed mutex) but only on recoverable-error paths, no UB.
vet.notes: Scope correction to the report: it scopes platforms to Linux/FreeType, but macOS is also affected — coretext Face's hb_font is a raw handle destroyed only in deinit (coretext.rs:163,346), so the get_face_from_entry set_size-error path and Collection-without-Drop error exits leak the HarfBuzz font on macOS too; only the CTFont and DeferredFace CoreText payload are RAII. Conversely the report is right that Collection::add's missing internal errdefer is upstream-inherited (Ghostty's add also lacks it), so that sub-site is supporting evidence only; fixing it anyway is a small, safe over-delivery.

findings.title: WebCanvas returns RGBA bytes through an atlas ABI declared BGRA
findings.replay_cell: upheld

vet.evidence: Reproduced on current main (d34cc15, one bookkeeping commit past audit pin dc054bb; code unchanged). (1) crates/rustty-font/src/atlas.rs:62-67: Format::Bgra=2 documented "4 bytes per pixel BGRA", matching ghostty src/font/Atlas.zig:53-68 (grayscale/bgr/bgra only — NO rgba). (2) crates/rustty-font-shaper/src/face/web_canvas.rs:415-419: render_glyph maps `Format::Bgra => render.bitmap.clone()` with its own comment "Bitmap is already in RGBA (canvas ImageData order)"; ffi doc at :122 and .port/tools/web-canvas-glue.mjs:105 confirm getImageData RGBA. No swizzle anywhere (grep bgra|rgba over the file). (3) crates/rustty-web-canvas/src/lib.rs:84,91: release C ABI maps tag 2 → Format::Bgra, "2=BGRA", and exports atlas create/readback. (4) BGRA is semantically load-bearing: opengl_impl.rs:632-638 uploads Bgra atlases as gltex::Format::BGRA/SRGBA; metal_impl.rs:660-665 as MTLPixelFormat::BGRA8Unorm_sRGB. So red [255,0,0,255] stored unchanged reads as blue to any format-honoring consumer. (5) Oracle: ghostty src/font/face/web_canvas.zig:199-217 switches on `.rgba`, a variant absent from its own Atlas.zig enum — pinned upstream browser path is abandoned/uncompilable legacy (DEFERRALS.md:5430-5436), so the binding contract is Rustty's own declared ABI, which its bytes violate. No doc records the RGBA-in-BGRA mismatch as deliberate; DEFERRALS.md:5400,5437,5464 record web_canvas as DONE/browser-verified (grayscale demo).
vet.fix_plan: In crates/rustty-font-shaper/src/face/web_canvas.rs render_glyph (:415-419), replace `Format::Bgra => render.bitmap.clone()` with a swizzle producing true BGRA: copy the RGBA bitmap swapping bytes 0 and 2 of each 4-byte pixel (alpha/green unchanged). Implement as a small pure helper (e.g. `fn rgba_to_bgra(px: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8>`) so it is unit-testable off-wasm; update the arm comment/file-head PORT NOTE to record this as faithful divergence #4 (reference's `.rgba` arm cannot compile against the pinned Atlas enum; the modern enum's only 4-byte format is BGRA, so convert RGBA→BGRA to honor the declared ABI and the OpenGL/Metal BGRA uploads). Behavioral delta: a format-2 atlas readback of an opaque-red Canvas pixel changes from [255,0,0,255] to [0,0,255,255]; grayscale path untouched. Proof: host unit test on the helper (red/green/blue/alpha vectors incl. the non-symmetric red control), plus rerun the existing dynamic probe shape (node wave9-webcanvas-color-order.mjs against the rebuilt rustty_web_canvas.wasm) expecting [0,0,255,255]. Ghostty has no test here (path is dead upstream); adding one is in-plan.
vet.severity_assessment: Agree P3: real color-order defect in a shipped public C ABI, but latent — current demo/harness uses grayscale atlases, and the whole web_canvas backend is a beyond-plan user-requested resurrection of dead upstream code.
vet.notes: Report is accurate and appropriately hedged. Nuances: (a) there is no working upstream oracle — pinned ghostty web_canvas.zig references a nonexistent `.rgba` Atlas variant, so the "contract" is Rustty's own Format::Bgra declaration plus its renderers' BGRA texture uploads; the fix is a fidelity-consistent correction, not a byte-for-byte oracle match. (b) The in-file comment at web_canvas.rs:416-418 shows the porter knowingly stored RGBA under the Bgra arm (mirroring the reference's `.rgba` arm) but never documented the ABI mismatch as a deferral — file-head FAITHFUL DIVERGENCES list (items 1-3) omits it. (c) rustty-web-canvas/src/lib.rs needs no code change; only its "2=BGRA" doc stays true once the swizzle lands.

fix.detail: render_glyph's 4-byte-atlas arm now swizzles Canvas RGBA -> BGRA via a new pure `rgba_to_bgra` helper instead of `render.bitmap.clone()`; file-head FAITHFUL DIVERGENCES gained item 4 (the reference's `.rgba` arm names a variant absent from its own Atlas.zig enum, so Rustty's declared Format::Bgra + the GL/Metal BGRA uploads are the binding contract). Grayscale (A8) arm untouched. Proving gate: web-canvas-instantiate.mjs (c5) renders into a format-2 atlas with a mock canvas painting opaque RED and asserts readback [0,0,255,255]; pre-fix .wasm FAILED with [255,0,0,255], post-fix GREEN. Module is wasm-only, so no host #[test] can reach it (same constraint the WS19 DeferredFace row documents).

Proving harness: sh .port/tools/build-web-canvas-wasm.sh --release && node .port/tools/web-canvas-instantiate.mjs -> ALL OK (11 checks); pre-fi

I parsed the fixture bytes myself: Ghostty pkg/wuffs/src/too_big.png IHDR and too_big.jpg SOF both declare 32769x32768 -> 4,295,098,368 RGBA bytes = limit+131,072 (near-threshold). Rustty substitutes: test_fixtures.rs:40-41 generates PNG IHDR 65536x65536 -> 17,179,869,184; fixtures/too_big.jpg SOF0 patched to 65535x65535 -> 17,179,344,900 (parsed). Both exceed 8 GiB (8,589,934,592), so a guard widened to 8 GiB still rejects both fixtures and both tests stay green — the mutation-insensitivity holds by arithmetic, matching the report's worktree mutant run (wave-14-binary-assets.md:209-237, independently upheld in wave-14-binary-assets-independent-review.md:38,152-184). lib.rs:197 only pins the constant, not the guards' effective threshold. The blob substitution itself was a deliberate design instruction (RENDERER_BG_IMAGE_DESIGN.md:365-373,535-540: do NOT check in the 12.5 MB blob; F5 = 1x1 fixtures absent from checkout), but nothing mandated 16 GiB dimensions — near-threshold 32769x32768 declared dims fit the same tiny-fixture strategy.

(1) test_fixtures.rs:40-41: change generated PNG IHDR width to 32769, height to 32768 (0x00008001/0x00008000) so declared RGBA size = 4,295,098,368 = 4 GiB + 131,072, matching the oracle fixture exactly; update the doc comment at :25. (2) fixtures/too_big.jpg: re-patch the SOF0 dimension fields from 65535x65535 to height=32768, width=32769 (SOF stores height then width), or drop the binary and synthesize the patched header in-test like the PNG; update PORT NOTE at jpeg.rs:241-244 and png.rs:250-252. (3) Optionally add a threshold-matrix unit asserting 32769*32768*4 > MAXIMUM_IMAGE_SIZE while 32768*32768*4 == MAXIMUM_IMAGE_SIZE (arithmetic only, no decode) to pin the comparison operator. Proof: both too_big tests still pass unmodified (Overflow fires in decode_image_config before any allocation, so the near-threshold size is never allocated); a local mutant widening either guard to 8 GiB now flips both tests red (4,295,098,368 < 8 GiB), restoring the oracle's discrimination the report demonstrated was lost.

findings.title: resource generation does not enforce the declared gettext locale set

findings.title: `rustty-vaxis` stores panic-recovery TTY state but never installs Ghostty/libvaxis's panic recovery path
findings.replay_cell: independently upheld with oracle correction: Rustty ports libvaxis 0.5.1, whose cached oracle has the same panic recovery design; live pty crash probe was safe but inconclusive

vet.evidence: Reproduced on current main (d34cc15). rustty-vaxis stores panic-restore state but has no consumer: crates/rustty-vaxis/src/tty.rs:86-97 GlobalTty {fd, termios} is #[allow(dead_code)] with comment "that handler is not yet ported, so they are write-only for now"; tty.rs:277 writes GLOBAL_TTY in PosixTty::init; grep of crates/rustty-vaxis/src for set_hook/take_hook/recover finds nothing — GLOBAL_TTY (private, tty.rs:103) is never read. Oracle libvaxis 0.5.1 (~/.cache/zig/p/vaxis-0.5.1-BWNV_Los.../src/main.zig:50-78) exports Panic.call=panic_handler; recover() writes csi_u_pop+mouse_reset+bp_reset+rmcup and deinits global_tty; ghostty's vendored 0.6.0 matches. So the library-surface gap is real. CRITICAL correction both prior reports missed: Ghostty itself NEVER installs vaxis's panic recovery — repo-wide grep of /Users/gael/projects/ghostty/src for "vaxis.Panic|vaxis.recover|panic_handler|pub const panic" returns zero hits (all src/main*.zig checked); Zig panic overrides are root-module decls, so Ghostty binaries use the default panic handler and a panic in list-themes leaves the terminal raw in Ghostty too. Runtime behavior therefore already matches the oracle; the gap is only the unported recover()/panic_handler library functions of the vendored subset.
vet.fix_plan: Port libvaxis 0.5.1 main.zig:66-78 recover() as pub fn rustty_vaxis::recover(): read GLOBAL_TTY (add a read path in crates/rustty-vaxis/src/tty.rs — drop #[allow(dead_code)], add a crate-visible take/with accessor), write ctlseqs::CSI_U_POP+MOUSE_RESET+BP_RESET+RMCUP via libc::write to the stored fd, then tcsetattr(TCSAFLUSH) the saved termios (the Zig gty.deinit() equivalent). Expose the Zig Panic export as a documented opt-in installer (pub fn install_panic_recovery() using std::panic::set_hook chaining the previous hook) but do NOT install it in rustty-cli — Ghostty never installs vaxis.Panic, so auto-installing would diverge from the oracle. Proving test: in-crate test using the TestTty/pipe pattern (tty.rs already has TestTty) seeding GLOBAL_TTY with a pipe fd, calling recover(), asserting the exact reset byte bundle arrives on the read end; termios-restore arm asserted via a pty fd where available.
vet.deferral_ref: In-code explicit deferral marker only: crates/rustty-vaxis/src/tty.rs:90-91 ("stored for a future panic-time restore ... that handler is not yet ported, so they are write-only for now"). No entry in .port/phase-2/DEFERRALS.md, VAXIS_C3B_DESIGN.md, or VAXIS_C4A_DESIGN.md (grepped panic/recover/global_tty); CLI_BLUEPRINT.md §RUNTIME-DEFERRED covers vaxis TUI paths generally but predates the vaxis port and does not name the panic handler. Not a macOS-first platform deferral — the affected paths are POSIX/macOS-reachable.
vet.severity_assessment: Agree P4, arguably overstated: runtime behavior already matches Ghostty (which never installs vaxis.Panic), so this is a library-surface fidelity gap, not a behavioral divergence.
vet.notes: Both the wave report and the independent review treated the missing panic hook as a reachable behavioral gap ("Rustty takes the ordinary Rust panic path" in list-themes/list-keybinds/list-colors/vxfw). That framing is wrong on the oracle side: Zig panic handlers activate only via a root-module `pub const panic`/`Panic` declaration, and no file in ghostty/src declares one or references vaxis.Panic/recover — so Ghostty's CLI TUI panics also bypass vaxis recovery and leave the terminal raw. The confirmed gap is narrower than reported: rustty-vaxis has not ported the recover()/panic_handler library functions of vendored libvaxis 0.5.1 (GLOBAL_TTY write-only, self-documented at tty.rs:90-91). The review's 0.5.1-vs-0.6.0 oracle correction is accurate (verified: 0.5.1 cache main.zig:55-78 matches the cited design). The review's pty probe was inconclusive, as it itself states. Fix should port the library surface without auto-installing the hook, to avoid over-fixing past the oracle.

fix.detail: Ported libvaxis 0.5.1 main.zig:66-78 recover() as pub rustty_vaxis::recover() (POSIX + Windows arms) and main.zig:50-64 Panic/panic_handler as OPT-IN install_panic_recovery() (set_hook chaining the previous hook). tty.rs GlobalTty/GLOBAL_TTY lost #[allow(dead_code)] and became pub(crate) (POSIX + windows_tty twins); stale 'handler is not yet ported / write-only' PORT NOTE replaced. Per the vet correction, the hook is NOT auto-installed anywhere (ghostty declares no root-module panic override, so its binaries never install vaxis.Panic) — documented in a PORT NOTE. recover() writes csi_u_pop+mouse_reset+bp_reset+rmcup to the stored fd (abandoning the rest on a failed write = writeAll's error return), then inlines gty.deinit(): tcsetattr(TCSAFLUSH) of the saved termios + close except on macOS. Added a PORT NOTE for the one divergence: Zig writes via the tty's BUFFERED std.Io.Writer (may never flush), rustty writes the fd directly since the global holds only fd+termios. Windows arm mirrors WindowsTty::deinit exactly (SetConsoleOutputCP, 2x setConsoleMode, 2x CloseHandle) and was type-checked/clippy-clean via .port/phase-2/wincheck.sh (cfg-forced), not built for a real Windows target —
fix.tests_run: cargo test -p rustty-vaxis --lib -> 101 passed; 0 failed (includes the 3 new recover_tests). cargo test -p rustty-vaxis --lib recover_tests -> 3 passed; 0 failed. cargo check -p rustty-cli --lib -> Finished (green). cargo clippy -p rustty-vaxis --lib --all-targets -> zero diagnostics. cargo fmt -p rustty-vaxis -- --check -> clean. Windows arm: bash .port/phase-2/wincheck.sh + cargo clippy --manifest-path /tmp/wincheck-rustty-vaxis/Cargo.toml --all-targets -- -D warnings -> Finished, zero diagnostics (cfg-forced type-check only; real Windows build still environment-blocked).
fix.verify_problems: None blocking. Three minor observations, all non-blocking: (1) EINTR nit — the POSIX write loop in `recover()` aborts the bundle on `n <= 0`, whereas Zig's `std.posix.write` retries on `.INTR`; since the oracle's write is inside `catch {}` (all errors swallowed) and reaches the fd only if the buffered writer happens to drain, the observable difference is negligible, but it is a real error-handling divergence not called out in the PORT NOTE. (2) `install_panic_recovery_runs_recover_then_chains_previous_hook` asserts that both `recover()` and the previous hook ran, but does not assert the ORDER (`recover(); defaultPanic(...)`); it would still pass if the hook body were reordered. (3) The reset-bundle test builds `expected` from the same `ctlseqs` constants `recover()` uses, so it proves membership+order (the actual oracle claim from main.zig:69-73) but is tautological on each sequence's bytes — those are covered by the separate ctlseqs parity.

findings.title: Kitty color OSC 21 palette key parsing accepts `+1` as palette 1 in Rustty while Ghostty rejects the key via `std.fmt.parseUnsigned(u8, ..., 10)`
findings.replay_cell: independently upheld; no additional Kitty key/color gap

vet.evidence: Reproduced myself on main d34cc15 (git log dc054bb..HEAD shows zero commits to any cited file). W18 member: rustty-vt/src/kitty/color.rs:106 uses key.parse::<u8>(); oracle ghostty/src/terminal/kitty/color.zig:51 uses std.fmt.parseUnsigned(u8,key,10). My own probes (scratchpad, zig 0.16 + rustc): Rust "+1".parse::<u8>()=Ok(1), Zig parseUnsigned("+1")=InvalidCharacter; also NEW nuance: Zig accepts "1_2"=12,"2_5_5"=255, Rust rejects — so drift is bidirectional, not plus-only. Path-dep probe against workspace crates: Kind::parse("+1")=Some(Palette(1)); reachable via osc/parsers/kitty_color.rs:73. W19 member: rustty-vt/src/color.rs:133-162 parse_int_u8_base0 skips '_' anywhere and has no sign handling; oracle color.zig:63-70 uses parseInt(u8,trimmed,0). My probes: Zig accepts "+1"=1, rejects "_1","1_","_","0x_F","0b_10","0xF_"; Rustty probe: "+1=#AABBCC"=err InvalidFormat, "_1="ok:1, "1_="ok:1, "_="ok:0, "0x_F="ok:15, "0b_10="ok:2 — exact inversion. Reachable: config value_types.rs:2801 (Palette::parse_cli) and vt-c color.rs:259 / lib.rs:164 (rustty_color_parse_palette_entry) both delegate to the same VT helper. Also Zig "-1" base-0 → Overflow vs Rustty InvalidFormat (error-class only). Grepped DEFERRALS.md/MAIN_PARITY.md/INTEGRATION_PARITY.md/GAP_ANALYSIS.md: no deferral covers palette/kitty index parsing.
vet.fix_plan: Both fixes are rustty-vt-local; config and vt-c delegate so they inherit. (1) crates/rustty-vt/src/color.rs: rewrite parse_int_u8_base0 to faithful Zig parseInt(u8,s,0) semantics — optional leading +/- sign ('-' on nonzero u8 → Overflow), then 0x/0o/0b prefix detect, digits where '_' is legal only when preceded by a digit and not terminal (reject "_1","1_","_","0x_F","0b_10","0xF_"; accept "+1","1_2","0b1_0"). (2) crates/rustty-vt/src/kitty/color.rs Kind::parse: replace key.parse::<u8>() with a faithful parseUnsigned(u8,key,10) helper — no sign accepted, '_' separators between digits accepted (reject "+1"; accept "1_2"=12). Consider one shared helper in color.rs (parse_with_sign core, unsigned wrapper) used by both. Proving tests: rustty-vt unit tests asserting Kind::parse("+1")==None and Kind::parse("1_2")==Some(Palette(12)); parse_palette_entry("+1=#AABBCC") ok index 1, "_1=/1_=/_=/0x_F=/0b_10=" all InvalidFormat, "-1=#AABBCC" Overflow; one OSC-level test that "21;+1=?" yields no palette request; add matching cases to rustty-config palette_parse_cli and rustty-vt-c parse_palette_entry_invalid. Run: cargo test -p rustty-vt kitty::color + parse_palette_entry + osc_21_kitty_color_protocol; -p rustty-config palette_parse_cli; -p rustty-vt-c parse_palette_entry.
vet.severity_assessment: Agree: P4 for the W18 OSC-21 member (leniency drift, low impact); P3 for the W19 palette member (rejects Ghostty-valid config "palette = +1=#AABBCC" and accepts malformed forms via public C API) — group severity should read P3.
vet.notes: Report correction/extension: W18-B07-PLUS-01 is understated — the divergence is bidirectional. Ghostty's parseUnsigned(u8,...,10) accepts underscore digit separators ("1_2"→12, "2_5_5"→255) which Rust's str::parse rejects, so Rustty also REJECTS Ghostty-valid OSC 21 keys, not just accepts "+1". The two member rows are genuinely distinct surfaces (OSC 21 key via parseUnsigned base-10 vs config/C palette entry via parseInt base-0) but share one remediation shape: a faithful Zig std.fmt parser helper. Existing tests pass because they omit sign/underscore-placement cases, matching the report's claim.

fix.detail: Replaced the ad-hoc parse_int_u8_base0 and kitty key.parse::<u8>() with a faithful port of std.fmt.parseInt/parseUnsigned/parseIntWithSign/charToDigit (u8 monomorphization, u8 accumulator, '_' legal only between digits, '-' nonzero -> Overflow, base-0 prefix detect). Kind::parse now uses parse_unsigned_u8(key,10): '+1' -> None, '1_2' -> Palette(12). Verified byte-for-byte against zig 0.16 on a 26-case table (both parseInt base0 and parseUnsigned base10). rustty-config Palette::parse_cli and rustty-vt-c rustty_color_parse_palette_entry inherit via delegation.

Adjacent surface NOT touched (separate row, pre-existing, not a regression): crates/rustty-config/src/value_types.rs:2557 still has its own independent ad-hoc `parse_int_u8_base0`/`parse_unsigned_base0` (u128 accumulator, own sign/underscore rules) used by BackgroundBlur::Radius and other base-0 config ints — it does not delegate to the new faithful rustty-vt helper, so std.fmt.parseInt fidelity there is unverified.

findings.title: promised offline/self-contained source archive lacks Cargo vendor inputs
findings.replay_cell: upheld; normalized from legacy `High` as packaging/source-distribution defect

vet.evidence: Reproduced on current main (no changes to PACKAGING.md or xtask/src/dist.rs since audit pin dc054bb; `git log dc054bb..HEAD -- PACKAGING.md xtask/src/dist.rs` empty). PACKAGING.md:87-99 promises release source tarballs "already ship with a vendor/ directory and a .cargo/config.toml ... the tarball is already self-contained and the build below runs fully offline", and PACKAGING.md:53-55 repeats "a vendored dependency tree". But xtask/src/dist.rs:45-81 builds the archive purely via `git archive HEAD` + one `--add-file` for the staged VERSION file (dist.rs:64-76); it never runs `cargo vendor` and injects no `vendor/` or `.cargo/config.toml`. Neither path exists on disk or in tracked files (`ls vendor .cargo` -> No such file; `git ls-files | grep '^(vendor/|\.cargo/)'` empty). distcheck (dist.rs:118-123) claims to "prove it is self-contained" but runs plain `cargo build --workspace` with no `--offline`/`--locked` and the user's default CARGO_HOME, so network/cache masks the missing vendor tree. Oracle: ghostty/src/build/GhosttyDist.zig:24-38,61-79 injects each generated dist resource and :149-153 addCheckFile-asserts each is present in the extracted archive — promised dist-only inputs are injected AND asserted; Rustty does neither for its promised Cargo inputs. Not covered by any parity/deferral doc (grep of DEFERRALS/MAIN_PARITY/INTEGRATION_PARITY/GAP_ANALYSIS for dist/tarball/vendor: no hit).
vet.fix_plan: Files: xtask/src/dist.rs (only code change needed). Behavioral delta: (1) dist(): instead of writing the tar.gz directly, pipe `git archive --format=tar --prefix=rustty-<v>/ HEAD` into an extraction under a temp stage dir (git archive --add-file cannot inject a multi-thousand-file vendor tree), write VERSION, run `cargo vendor --locked <stage>/rustty-<v>/vendor` capturing stdout into `<stage>/rustty-<v>/.cargo/config.toml`, then `tar czf dist/rustty-<v>.tar.gz -C <stage> rustty-<v>` — matching the PACKAGING.md:87-99 contract and the GhosttyDist.zig pattern of injecting dist-only inputs. (2) distcheck(): after extraction, assert `vendor/` and `.cargo/config.toml` exist (mirroring GhosttyDist.zig:149-153 addCheckFile assertions), and build with `cargo build --workspace --offline --locked` with CARGO_HOME set to a fresh temp dir so a warm cache/network cannot mask a missing vendor tree. Proving test: a #[test] (ignored-by-default or xtask self-test lane, since it shells to git/cargo) that runs dist(), lists the tarball via `tar tzf`, and asserts `rustty-<v>/VERSION`, `rustty-<v>/vendor/` entries, and `rustty-<v>/.cargo/config.toml` are present; distcheck in CI proves the offline build. Ghostty has no equivalent unit test (its check is a build-graph step), so the added test is a permitted Rustty-side addition.
vet.severity_assessment: Agree with P4: real doc-vs-implementation packaging defect, but release-artifact publishing is not yet stood up so no shipped artifact is currently wrong.
vet.notes: Nuances: (a) PACKAGING.md:20-23 and :45-48 do defer the release-artifact host and tip pipeline to "release-infra (Batch 4)", and :143-147 defers the Nix path — but those cover publishing, not the content of the tarball xtask dist produces today; the vendor promise is written in the present tense and no deferral doc covers it, so known_deferred=false. (b) Report is correct that this is a promise-vs-implementation gap, not a structural oracle divergence: Ghostty's own PACKAGING.md:71-84 has packagers fetch Zig deps into an offline cache as step 1 (its tarball vendors generated resources, not dependencies), so Rustty's doc makes a stronger promise than the oracle and its implementation fulfills neither the promise nor the oracle's inject-and-assert pattern. An alternative smaller fix (amend PACKAGING.md to a Ghostty-style "run cargo vendor first" step) would also close the contradiction, but implementing vendoring matches the authored Rustty contract and keeps the offline property testable. (c) All report line cites checked and accurate on current main.

findings.title: MouseShape header parity test is self-derived from the descriptor under test and does not actually read the checked-in/generated header, though today's header list matches Ghostty
findings.replay_cell: independently upheld; no product/header data drift

vet.evidence: Reproduced on current main (d34cc15). Ghostty oracle: src/terminal/mouse.zig:96 calls lib.checkGhosttyHEnum(Shape,"GHOSTTY_MOUSE_SHAPE_"); src/lib/enum.zig:94-140 imports the real generated header (`const c = @import("ghostty.h")`) and checks @hasDecl + expectEqual against actual declarations. Rustty: crates/rustty-vt/src/mouse.rs:189-201 — the test builds `t = enum_descriptor()` then passes a closure that looks names up in `t.fields` itself (`fields.iter().find_map(... Some(*v as i64))`), so check_ghostty_henum (rustty-lib/src/enum.rs:138) compares the descriptor to itself; the checked-in header include/rustty-embed.h:686-721 (rustty_action_mouse_shape_e, 34 enumerators) is never read. Dropping/reordering a RUSTTY_MOUSE_SHAPE_* line cannot fail this test. Ran `cargo test -p rustty-vt --lib mouse::shape_tests` — passes (1 ok). No other gate covers enum declarations: .port/tools/gates/check_rustty_h_abi.sh checks API function name-sets only (its own comment), check_embed_h_abi.sh checks aggregate struct sizes only. No current data drift: header's 34 names/order match Shape variants (verified visually, values sequential 0..33), matching the primary's match=True probe. Not documented as a deferral — grep of DEFERRALS.md/MAIN_PARITY.md/INTEGRATION_PARITY.md/GAP_ANALYSIS.md has no henum entry; only inline PORT NOTEs. Same self-derived pattern recurs (osc/mod.rs:406 "mirroring the established checkGhosttyHEnum pattern (see mouse.rs Shape)", renderer, apprt-api, input/*).
vet.fix_plan: In crates/rustty-vt/src/mouse.rs shape_tests: replace the descriptor-derived closure with a lookup parsed from the checked-in header, mirroring Ghostty's @import("ghostty.h"). At test time read concat!(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"), "/../../include/rustty-embed.h"), extract the `rustty_action_mouse_shape_e` typedef enum block, parse enumerator names in order (supporting optional `= N`, else sequential from 0) into a HashMap<String,i64>, and pass `|name| map.get(name).copied()` to check_ghostty_henum. Behavioral delta vs oracle: the test then fails when the header drops, renames, reorders, or revalues any RUSTTY_MOUSE_SHAPE_* declaration — exactly what checkGhosttyHEnum guarantees in Ghostty. Optionally hoist the header-enum parser into rustty-lib/src/enum.rs (e.g. parse_header_enum(path, enum_name)) since osc/renderer/apprt-api call sites share the tautological pattern, but the minimal in-scope fix touches only mouse.rs. Proving test: the existing ghostty_h_mouse_shape test itself, plus a negative self-check (feed the parser a copy with one enumerator removed and assert Err) to prove the probe can fail.
vet.severity_assessment: Agree with P4: test-adequacy weakness only; header data currently matches the oracle, no product behavior affected.
vet.notes: Report is accurate on all probes. One addition: the weakness is systemic — every check_ghostty_henum call site in the port (osc progress state, renderer, apprt-api ipc/action, input key/mods) uses the same self-derived closure, and osc/mod.rs:357 explicitly cites mouse.rs as the established pattern; a shared parser fix would close the whole family, though this group's registry row scopes only the mouse test. Also note check_rustty_h_abi.sh keeps the header equal to the oracle-renamed umbrella at the function-symbol level only, so enum drift is genuinely unguarded today.

findings.title: `StringMap.string` uses plain `Vec<u8>` and comments/tests overstate Ghostty's `[:0]const u8` sentinel contract; current regex/link paths pass explicit byte bounds, so no current functional failure was verified
findings.replay_cell: independently corrected from primary P3

vet.evidence: Reproduced on current main (d34cc15; no commits since audit pin dc054bb touched these files; sha256 of string_map.rs:1-620 = 7272cfb3... identical to audit). Ghostty: StringMap.zig:20 `string: [:0]const u8`; Screen.zig:2919 `toOwnedSliceSentinel(0)`, :2922 `dupeZ(u8, text)` for map.string. Rustty: crates/rustty-vt/src/string_map.rs:45 `pub string: Vec<u8>`; PORT NOTE :43-44 claims the Vec "carr[ies] the NUL-terminated invariant"; screen.rs:4153+4169-4172 assigns plain `text.clone()` — no NUL byte is ever stored; screen.rs:4100-4114 repeats the overstated invariant claim. No functional failure: I traced the only live consumer path — string_map.rs:119-122 `search_with_param` → rustty-oniguruma/src/regex.rs:88 `search_impl` → :120-143 passes explicit `str_ptr`/`str_ptr.add(str.len())`/start/end to onig_search_with_param, exactly like Ghostty's oniguruma binding (ptr + ptr+len), so the sentinel is never observed. rustty-core surface.rs:9527-9581 (linkAtPin) goes through the same bounded API. Grep of string_map.rs tests and screen.rs:12378-12417 cleanup test: zero NUL/sentinel assertions — comments overstate, tests merely omit. DEFERRALS.md:312-322 covers only the oniguruma feature gating, not the sentinel representation; not a documented deferral. Agree with the independent review's P4 reclassification.
vet.fix_plan: Docs-only fix. (1) Rewrite the PORT NOTEs at crates/rustty-vt/src/string_map.rs:43-44 and crates/rustty-vt/src/screen.rs:4100-4114 to state the truth: `[:0]const u8` maps to an UNSENTINELED `Vec<u8>` whose length equals Ghostty's sentinel-exclusive logical length; no NUL byte is stored; parity holds because every consumer (rustty-oniguruma regex.rs onig_search start/end pointers) passes explicit byte bounds, mirroring Ghostty's binding. (2) Optionally add a `#[cfg(feature = "oniguruma")]` test asserting a match is found on an unsentineled buffer containing no interior/trailing NUL (codifies the audit probe) and that selection_string's map.string byte-equals the returned text. Explicitly do NOT append a 0 byte to the Vec: that would change `string.len()` and break offset/loop-bound parity in SearchIterator::next (string_map.rs:109) versus Zig's sentinel-exclusive `len`. Proof: cargo test -p rustty-vt string_map --features oniguruma stays green plus the new test.
vet.severity_assessment: Agree with corrected P4: real representation/comment drift, zero current behavioral divergence.
vet.notes: Two corrections to the reports: (a) the registry row says "comments/tests overstate" — only the comments overstate (string_map.rs:43-44, screen.rs:4100-4114); the tests simply never assert the sentinel (0 grep hits), which is omission, not overstatement. The Vec<u8> mapping itself is the locked byteslice convention (never lossy String), so the representation choice is plan-consistent; only the invariant wording is wrong.

findings.title: `removeByPtr` zero-sized-key fallback uses slot 0 even when a true ZST key hashes to another slot at capacity greater than one; Ghostty's named ZST test uses `i32`, and Rustty's current product callers use non-ZST `Offset<Cell>` keys
findings.replay_cell: independently found on replay; classified as shared generic correctness/test gap, not Rustty-only parity, with no product caller found

vet.evidence: On current main (d34cc15; hash_map.rs unchanged since audit pin dc054bb — git diff empty): crates/rustty-vt/src/hash_map.rs:1005-1009 sets idx=0 when size_of::<K>()==0, an exact port of ghostty src/terminal/hash_map.zig:882-886 (same "must be at index 0" comment). Insertion slot = hash & (cap-1) (hash_map.rs:573,664,824); AutoContext (hash_map.rs:144-149) uses DefaultHasher, and my no-dep rustc probe gives hash(())=15130871412783076140, mod16=12 — so a true ZST key at cap 16 occupies slot 12 while remove_by_ptr removes free slot 0: metadata for slot 12 stays used while size is decremented. Ghostty's test "HashMap removeByPtr 0 sized key" (hash_map.zig:1720-1721) uses AutoHashMapUnmanaged(i32,u64) — not a ZST — so it never exercises the fallback; Rustty's port carries a PORT NOTE stating exactly this (hash_map.rs:2025-2029). No product caller uses a ZST key: all 4 remove_by_ptr_context call sites (page_impl.rs:2004,2208,2410,2442) go through GraphemeMap (page.rs:115-118) and hyperlink::Map (hyperlink.rs:57), both keyed by non-ZST Offset<Cell>. The bug exists identically in the oracle (audit's Zig probe reproduced "expected 456, found null" on Ghostty), so this is a shared latent generic bug, NOT a Rustty-vs-Ghostty parity divergence. Not mentioned in DEFERRALS.md/MAIN_PARITY.md/GAP_ANALYSIS.md (grep for zst/zero-sized only hits unrelated placeholder ZSTs).
vet.fix_plan: Single file: crates/rustty-vt/src/hash_map.rs. In remove_by_ptr_context (line ~1005), replace the ZST idx=0 fallback with a scan of the metadata for the unique used slot (for ZST K all keys are equal, so at most one entry exists; find i in 0..capacity where metadata[i].is_used() and pass that to remove_by_index_context), guarded by a PORT NOTE stating this deliberately diverges from the oracle's slot-0 fallback because the oracle path is provably wrong (Ghostty probe fails with a true void key) and unreachable by any product caller. Proving test: add HashMap_removeByPtr_true_zst_key using AutoHashMapUnmanaged<(), u32, 100> at layout capacity 16 (mirrors the audit's Zig probe): put ((),123), get_key_ptr, remove_by_ptr_context, assert count()==0 and get_context(())==None, then re-put ((),456) and assert get==Some(456); this test fails on current main (stale used slot 12) and passes with the scan fix. Run: cargo test -p rustty-vt hash_map. Alternative if strict oracle fidelity is preferred: keep code as-is and only add a #[ignore]-annotated red test + DEFERRALS.md row documenting the shared upstream bug (fix_category docs) — but the scan fix is invisible to every product caller and strictly safer.
vet.severity_assessment: Agree with P4: latent shared generic bug with zero product callers (all keys are non-ZST Offset<Cell>), no user-visible impact.
vet.notes: Registry framing is accurate: this is a shared generic correctness/test-coverage gap inherited from the oracle (Ghostty's terminal hash_map derives from Zig std HashMapUnmanaged, which has the same idx=0 ZST fallback), not a Rustty-only parity divergence — Rustty faithfully mirrors the oracle including the bug. "Confirmed" here means the reported facts reproduce on current main, not that port fidelity is broken. One correction/nuance to the independent review: its Rust-side ZST cargo probe never completed (network/disk limits); my DefaultHasher probe independently confirms mod16=12, closing that limitation. The misleadingly-named test is already documented in-tree via PORT NOTE at hash_map.rs:2025-2029.

findings.title: Direct Kitty graphics command parser error classification differs for unsigned negative fields: Rustty maps values such as `i=-1` to `InvalidFormat`, while Ghostty's unsigned parser returns `Overflow`; APC/product response behavior remains aligned because invalid commands are dropped without response
findings.replay_cell: independently upheld; no other B02 findings found

vet.evidence: File unchanged since audit pin: `git log dc054bb..HEAD -- crates/rustty-vt/src/kitty/graphics_command.rs` is empty (HEAD d34cc15). Rustty routes all non-z/H/V fields through parse_int_u32 (graphics_command.rs:362-365), which maps every non-overflow ParseIntError kind to Error::InvalidFormat (:391-402). Ghostty uses `try std.fmt.parseInt(u32, ...)` (graphics_command.zig:289-292 in finishValue). I probed both primitives myself: Rust `"-1".parse::<u32>()` -> InvalidDigit (so Rustty returns InvalidFormat); Zig 0.16 `std.fmt.parseInt(u32,"-1",10)` -> error.Overflow; also `-4294967295`/`-99999999999` -> Overflow, `"-0"` -> Ok(0), bare `"-"`/empty -> InvalidCharacter. So Rustty diverges for negative text in unsigned fields (InvalidFormat vs Overflow) AND for `"-0"` (Rustty InvalidFormat vs Ghostty Ok(0) — a nuance the report missed). Impact contained: apc/mod.rs:329-335 discards any parser error (None), matching Ghostty apc.zig catch->null, so no APC/response/user-visible divergence; direct-parser API only. No existing Rustty test asserts the wrong kind (only positive-u32/negative-i32 overflow tests at :1661-1680, mirroring Ghostty's zig tests at 1259/1270). DEFERRALS.md kitty entries concern Screen-dependent files (resolved), nothing about parser error classification — not a documented deferral.
vet.fix_plan: In crates/rustty-vt/src/kitty/graphics_command.rs, make parse_int_u32 mirror Zig parseWithSign for unsigned: if slice starts with b'-', parse the remaining digits as u32 magnitude (digit/empty errors -> InvalidFormat, PosOverflow -> Overflow), then return Ok(0) for magnitude 0 and Err(Error::Overflow) for any nonzero magnitude; leave the non-negative path unchanged. Proving tests (add to the file's tests module): `a=p,i=-1` and `a=p,p=-1` -> Err(Error::Overflow); `a=p,i=-0,q=2` completes with image id 0; existing ensure_proper_overflow_error_for_u32/i32 stay green. Run `cargo test -p rustty-vt kitty::graphics_command`.
vet.severity_assessment: Agree with P4: direct-parser error-kind mismatch only; APC layer drops errored commands identically on both sides, no user-visible behavior change.
vet.notes: W32-B02-PARSER-01 upheld exactly as written. Addition: the same Rustty code also misclassifies "-0" (Ghostty accepts it as 0 via parseInt negation; Rustty rejects InvalidFormat) — same root cause, covered by the same fix. Signed z/H/V fields are unaffected (parse_int_i32 handles NegOverflow -> Overflow correctly, bit-pattern storage matches @bitCast). Zig probe ran on zig 0.16.0; behavior matches the audit's pinned-toolchain observation and Zig's stable parseWithSign semantics.

fix.detail: Verifier's rejection confirmed against the oracle and fixed. parse_int_u32 now peels exactly one '-' byte (matching parseIntWithGenericCharacter) and delegates to a new byte-for-byte port of parseIntWithSign(u32, u8, buf, 10, .neg), so the first-digit `math.cast(u32, -digit) orelse error.Overflow` fires BEFORE the rest of the buffer is scanned: `-1a`, `-1_2`, `-1 ` now return Overflow (previously InvalidFormat via `magnitude.parse::<u32>()`). The oracle's pre-loop leading/trailing `_` rejection is reproduced in the right order (so `-1_` stays InvalidFormat while `-1_2` is Overflow), `_` is skipped mid-magnitude (`-0_0` -> Ok(0)), and the ad-hoc double-sign guard was removed because the faithful charToDigit loop already classifies `--1`/`-+1` as InvalidFormat. Non-negative path unchanged. Test `double_sign_is_invalid_format_for_u32` was renamed/widened to `invalid_format_cases_for_negative_u32`; a bare `i=-` was moved out of the parser-level test into the direct table test because finish_value (like the reference) short-circuits a single non-digit byte and never calls the integer parser on it. macOS-only code, no Linux dependency.

findings.title: Kitty graphics exported-symbol wiring matched for 16 symbols, header reachability, platform gates, and declared selectors; independent replay found out-of-range raw selector safe-build behavior differs for three direct getters
findings.replay_cell: independently corrected; see W33-B02-SELECTOR-01

vet.evidence: Reproduced by close reading on current main (d34cc15; `git diff --stat dc054bbc..HEAD -- crates/rustty-vt-c/` empty, so identical to audit pin). Rustty: rustty_kitty_graphics_get (crates/rustty-vt-c/src/lib.rs:1610), image_get (:1645), placement_get (:1747) each take the selector as raw c_int and narrow via from_c_int, returning Result::InvalidValue (-2) on None; Data::from_c_int (crates/rustty-vt-c/src/kitty_graphics.rs:143-149) maps only 0..=2, so 99->None (PlacementData :187, ImageData :379 likewise). Ghostty oracle: get (src/terminal/c/kitty_graphics.zig:101), image_get (:209), placement_get (:343) take enum-typed params and `switch (data)` directly, so raw 99 is a corrupt enum tag — safe builds panic "switch on corrupt value" (matches audit's probe exits 134), ReleaseFast is UB. Control matches: placement_iterator_set (kitty_graphics.zig:296-307) has an explicit std.enums.fromInt runtime-safety guard returning .invalid_value, mirrored by Rustty lib.rs:1711-1724 — both return -2. The Rustty behavior is deliberate, documented policy: D11 gate "no closed #[repr(C)] enum is received by value across the C ABI" (.port/phase-3/README.md:157, check_closed_enum_abi.sh, owner P3-W6 T2) and kitty_graphics.rs:134-141 explains an out-of-range #[repr(C)] enum param is UB in the callee prologue before any check can run. No Rust-side test currently pins the out-of-range-selector -2 contract (grep of rustty-vt-c tests found none).
vet.fix_plan: Do NOT change behavior: matching the oracle here would mean aborting the process on invalid selector (Ghostty's abort is a Zig safety-check artifact, and its ReleaseFast behavior is UB — there is no defined oracle semantics to match), and Rust cannot receive a corrupt #[repr(C)] enum by value soundly; the InvalidValue return is the documented D11 policy. Remediation is a pinning test: add unit tests in crates/rustty-vt-c/src/kitty_graphics.rs (or a tests/ integration test) asserting Data::from_c_int(99)==None, ImageData::from_c_int(99)==None, PlacementData::from_c_int(99)==None, and FFI-level calls rustty_kitty_graphics_get/image_get/placement_get/placement_iterator_set with selector/option 99 all return RUSTTY_INVALID_VALUE (-2) — plus selector 0 (Invalid) also returning -2 as the matched in-range control. Prove with `cargo test -p rustty-vt-c <filter>`. Optionally record the divergence in a parity doc note next to the D11 gate row.
vet.severity_assessment: Agree with P4: only observable when a C caller passes an out-of-contract selector, and only vs a safety-enabled Ghostty build (fast builds are UB); Rustty's behavior is strictly safer and deliberate.
vet.notes: Member rows: W33-B02 itself (16-symbol export wiring, alias renames image->image_get_handle / placement_next->placement_iterator_next, header reachability, no OS gates) re-checked and still matches — the only divergence is the SELECTOR-01 subcase. The report is accurate, including its placement_iterator_set matched-control claim (Ghostty has an explicit fromInt guard there because its param would otherwise also be corrupt-switch UB). Not a macOS-first platform deferral (known_deferred=false), but it IS a deliberately documented divergence under the D11 closed-enum-ABI doctrine (.port/phase-3/README.md:157; code comments cite D11/P3-W6 T2 and say PRE-EXISTING), so "confirmed divergence" should not be read as "port defect": returning RUSTTY_INVALID_VALUE dominates aborting/UB. The three getter exports' narrowing predates the Phase 3 resync per the in-code note.

Added kitty_graphics tests pinning from_c_int(99)/(-1)==None for Data/ImageData/PlacementData, in-range 0 accepted, and FFI-level rustty_kitty_graphics_get/image_get/placement_get/placement_iterator_set with 99 -> -2 plus selector 0 as the in-range control. findings.title: Allocator C convenience wrappers use the supplied allocator for normal nonzero calls, but Rustty calls the raw allocator surface with zero-length callbacks and `ret_addr=0` where Ghostty typed helpers short-circuit zero lengths and pass `@returnAddress()`

vet.evidence: Reproduced by close reading on current main (files unchanged since pin dc054bb: git diff dc054bb..HEAD empty for both allocator files; last touch 5c810ce5). Rustty: crates/rustty-vt-c/src/allocator.rs:35 calls allocator.alloc(len, Alignment(0), 0) and :62 allocator.free(ZigSlice, Alignment(0), 0) unconditionally; for a custom C allocator, CAllocatorAsZig forwards straight to the C vtable with the given len and ra=0 (crates/rustty-lib/src/allocator.rs:210-221, 251-262). Ghostty: src/terminal/c/Allocator.zig:16 allocator.alloc(u8, len) and :32 allocator.free(mem[0..len]) are Zig typed helpers; I verified in Zig 0.16.0 stdlib (Ghostty pins minimum_zig_version 0.16.0) that std/mem/Allocator.zig:295-299 returns a non-null aligned sentinel for byte_count==0 WITHOUT calling rawAlloc, :443-449 returns before rawFree when len==0, and :197-198/:449 pass @returnAddress() on nonzero paths. So custom C allocators observe: (1) zero-length alloc/free callbacks Ghostty never issues, (2) rustty_alloc(alloc,0) can return NULL (whatever the callback returns) where Ghostty always returns non-null sentinel, (3) ret_addr=0 vs real return address. The pinned runtime probe (.port/codex/evidence/w36-b06-allocator-independent/verification-log.md:60-68) showed exactly this; code is identical now. Only the DEFAULT-allocator path short-circuits zero length (rustty-lib/src/allocator.rs:366-371,390-393). No deferral doc mentions it (grep of DEFERRALS/MAIN_PARITY/INTEGRATION_PARITY/GAP_ANALYSIS: no hits).

Then crates/rustty-vt-c/src/allocator.rs:35 and :62 call these helpers instead of the raw trait methods. vet.evidence: Reproduced all raw facts on current main (no commits since pin dc054bb touched either file). Rustty include/rustty/vt/unicode.h:87-88 says "Returns 0 if and only if len is 0; otherwise consumes at least one codepoint"; :139 says cps "may be NULL only when len is 0". Ghostty oracle include/ghostty/vt/unicode.h:87-88,139 is WORD-FOR-WORD IDENTICAL modulo the ghostty->rustty rename. Both implementations tolerate cps==NULL && len>0 by writing width=0 and returning 0: ghostty src/terminal/c/unicode.zig:20-23 (cps orelse {out.*=0; return 0;}) and rustty crates/rustty-vt-c/src/unicode.rs:28-34 (exact structural mirror). Neither project has a test for (NULL, len>0): ghostty unicode.zig:50-83 and rustty unicode.rs:59-103 (oracle-tagged 65e61282a) test only (null,0), null-width, out-of-range, emoji. Therefore there is NO Rustty<->Ghostty divergence: header, behavior, and test surface are all parity-perfect. The prose is a caller precondition (documented contract narrower than the defensive total implementation) — Ghostty's own upstream design, faithfully inherited. Not listed in DEFERRALS.md/MAIN_PARITY.md as a gap; MAIN_PARITY.md:217 records 65e61282a as PORTED.
vet.severity_assessment: Disagree even with P4: no parity divergence exists; at most an upstream Ghostty doc-design nit inherited by the port's locked full-fidelity mandate.
vet.notes: The report's individual facts are correct (header prose, NULL-tolerant impls in both projects) but its classification as a Rustty gap is wrong: Rustty matches the oracle byte-for-byte in header prose and implementation. A doc contract stricter than defensive implementation behavior is not a misstatement — behavior outside a stated precondition is unspecified tolerance, and neither project tests or exports it as contract. Editing Rustty's header alone would CREATE a divergence from the oracle header, violating rename-fidelity. If upstream Ghostty ever relaxes its header prose, Rustty should mirror that commit; optionally a Rustty-only test pinning the (NULL, len>0)->0/width=0 defensive behavior could be added without touching the header, but that is enhancement, not gap remediation.

findings.title: `rustty_key_event_set_utf8` copies caller bytes into Rust-owned storage, so `rustty_key_event_get_utf8` returns a different pointer and does not reflect later caller-buffer mutation, while Ghostty stores the caller slice and its getter returns/observes the live source buffer
findings.replay_cell: independently found by B02 and coordinator replayed with paired Rustty/Ghostty C probes; allocator/OOM aspect is duplicate context, not the standalone root

vet.evidence: Reproduced by close reading on current main (d34cc15; key_event.rs unchanged since audit pin). Rustty crates/rustty-vt-c/src/key_event.rs:192-199 set_utf8 does `(*event_).event.utf8 = slice.to_vec()` (copy into Rust-owned Vec); get_utf8 at key_event.rs:210-224 returns `utf8.as_ptr()` of that Vec (null when empty). Ghostty oracle src/terminal/c/key_event.zig:103-106 stores the caller slice (`event.utf8 = ptr[0..len]`) and :108-111 get_utf8 returns `event.utf8.ptr` — the caller's own pointer, so later caller-buffer mutation is observable; Rustty's copy is not the same pointer and freezes the bytes at set time. Root cause: rustty-vt's KeyEvent owns `utf8: Vec<u8>` (crates/rustty-vt/src/input/key.rs, PORT NOTE "Stored as Vec<u8> so the event owns its text"). The divergence is DELIBERATE and documented in-source: key_event.rs:33-38 PORT NOTE claims it is "observationally identical for the C API ... tests compare bytes, not pointer identity" — that claim is falsified for pointer identity/live mutation (the audit's paired C probes printed same_pointer=0/reflects_source_mutation=0 for Rustty vs 1/1 for Ghostty; I did not rerun them, source semantics are unambiguous). Header include/rustty/vt/key/event.h:438-439 keeps Ghostty's borrow contract ("does NOT take ownership ... caller must ensure the string remains valid"). Not in DEFERRALS.md/MAIN_PARITY/INTEGRATION_PARITY/GAP_ANALYSIS (grepped: no key_event utf8 row).
vet.fix_plan: vt-c-local, no rustty-vt change. In crates/rustty-vt-c/src/key_event.rs: add `utf8_ptr: *const u8, utf8_len: usize` to KeyEventWrapper (init null/0 in new); set_utf8 stores the raw caller ptr/len instead of copying; get_utf8 writes utf8_len through len and returns utf8_ptr (null when len==0/ptr null) — exact Ghostty pointer/liveness behavior. For the internal encoder consumer (key_encode.rs:312 event_ref), rematerialize live bytes at use time: before taking the shared borrow, refresh `(*event_).event.utf8` from utf8_ptr/utf8_len via the raw pointer (or have event_ref do it), so encoding also observes post-set caller mutation like Ghostty's borrowed slice. Update the moved `set`/`get`/`complete_key_event` tests only if they rely on copy semantics (they compare bytes; they should still pass). Proving test: new #[test] in key_event.rs — set_utf8 on a mutable buffer, assert get_utf8 returns the buffer's own pointer, mutate the buffer, assert get_utf8 (and rustty_key_encoder_encode output) reflect the mutation. Note: this reinstates the caller-lifetime hazard, but that is the documented header contract (event.h:438-439) and full-fidelity per the port charter; the current safer copy is a defensible R4 divergence if the team prefers to keep it — then the remediation is instead to document it as a Justified R1 Divergence in DEFERRALS.md and fix the false "observationally identical" PORT NOTE.
vet.severity_assessment: Agree P4 — bytes are identical for conforming callers; only pointer-identity/live-mutation reliance diverges, and Rustty's behavior is strictly safer.
vet.notes: Report is accurate, including its dedupe of the allocator/OOM aspect (the Vec allocation bypassing RusttyAllocator is allocator-family, not this row). One correction to Rustty's own in-source claim, not the report: key_event.rs:33-38 asserts the copy is observationally identical, which is false at the C surface. findings.title: `rustty_formatter_terminal_new` validates an invalid non-null selection before allocating its formatter wrapper, so a successful custom allocator observes zero callbacks, while Ghostty allocates `FormatterWrapper`, installs `errdefer alloc.destroy(ptr)`, then returns `invalid_value` from `sel.toZig()` with one allocation and one cleanup free

vet.evidence: Verified on current main (HEAD d34cc15; `git log dc054bb..HEAD -- crates/rustty-vt-c/src/formatter.rs` is empty, so the audit's probe results still apply). Ghostty oracle src/terminal/c/formatter.zig: terminal null-check at :135, `alloc.create(FormatterWrapper)` at :138, `errdefer alloc.destroy(ptr)` at :140, selection `sel.toZig() orelse return error.InvalidValue` at :150-152 — so for a non-null terminal + invalid selection, a custom allocator observes exactly one alloc and one free before InvalidValue. Rustty crates/rustty-vt-c/src/formatter.rs `terminal_new_`: null-check :351-353, selection validated :363-372, emit validated :378-381 (D11 narrowing), and `cwrap::create` (the only allocator-callback site, cwrap.rs:39) is called only afterwards at :394-402 — zero allocator callbacks on the invalid-selection path. Public rc (-2/InvalidValue) and nulled handle match (:316-325). The audit's C probe (.port/codex/evidence/w90-b06-replay/evidence.md) measured valid case alloc=1 free=1 vs invalid selection alloc=0 free=0, consistent with my source reading. No deferral covers this: .port/phase-2/DEFERRALS.md formatter entries (:66-84) are all RESOLVED items about formatter tests/TerminalFormatter, not C-ABI allocator callback ordering.
vet.fix_plan: In crates/rustty-vt-c/src/formatter.rs `terminal_new_` (:345-408), mirror the oracle's alloc-then-validate order: after the terminal null check, obtain the wrapper allocation first (add a small `cwrap::alloc_uninit<T>(alloc_) -> *mut T` helper next to create/destroy at cwrap.rs:39-73, calling the same allocator callback without initializing), returning OutOfMemory if null; then perform selection to_zig and emit validation, calling `cwrap::destroy`-style free (raw dealloc, no drop of uninit T) on the error paths before returning InvalidValue (faithful `errdefer alloc.destroy(ptr)`); finally `ptr.write(FormatterWrapper{...})` and return it. Behavioral delta: for non-null terminal with invalid selection (and invalid emit), a custom allocator observes exactly 1 alloc + 1 free instead of 0/0; rc and handle unchanged; valid path unchanged (still 1 alloc). Proving test: a #[test] in formatter.rs mod tests using a counting CAllocator (pattern already exists for lifecycle tests) that passes a non-null terminal plus a CSelection whose grid refs cannot convert to pins, asserts rc == InvalidValue, handle null, alloc_count == 1, free_count == 1; plus a null-terminal case asserting 0/0. Existing terminal_new tests (:642, :683) must stay green.
vet.severity_assessment: Agree with P4: rc and handle match; only custom-allocator callback counts on an error path diverge.
vet.notes: Single-member group; the INDEX.md row (:1104) accurately describes the gap. One nuance the report omits: Rustty's extra `opts.emit` c_int validation (D11 narrowing, formatter.rs:378-381) also runs pre-alloc; Ghostty cannot express an invalid emit (typed enum ABI), so the fix should place that check after allocation too so every non-null-terminal error path shows 1 alloc + 1 free. The wrapper storing rebuild-inputs instead of a live formatter (PORT NOTE :374-376) does not affect this finding.

fix.detail: formatter::terminal_new_ now mirrors formatter.zig:135-152: terminal null check -> allocate the FormatterWrapper -> fallible narrowing -> ptr.write(). Both the selection to_zig arm and the port-only D11 emit narrowing free the storage before returning InvalidValue, so every non-null-terminal error path shows a custom allocator 1 alloc + 1 free (was 0/0); null-terminal stays 0/0. rc and out handle unchanged. findings.title: `clipboard-codepoint-map` wrapper formatting accepts overlong string replacements in Rustty through a growable buffer, while Ghostty serializes each wrapper entry through a fixed 1024-byte buffer and returns `OutOfMemory`/`NoSpaceLeft` past that boundary
findings.replay_cell: independently found by B04 and upheld by B05; Rustty boundary probe formatted replacement lengths 1017, 1018, and 1200, while Zig oracle accepted 1017 and rejected 1018/1200

vet.evidence: Oracle: ghostty src/config/Config.zig:8345-8384 — RepeatableClipboardCodepointMap.formatEntry serializes each entry via `var buf: [1024]u8` + `std.fmt.bufPrint(&buf, "U+{X:0>4}={s}"...) catch return error.OutOfMemory` (range form "U+{X:0>4}-U+{X:0>4}={s}"). So a string replacement making the serialized entry exceed 1024 bytes deterministically fails formatting (NoSpaceLeft→OutOfMemory); boundary = 1017 value bytes for a 4-hex-digit single codepoint (1024−7), matching the report's 1017-ok/1018-fail probe. Rustty current main: crates/rustty-config/src/value_types.rs:5398-5437 — format_entry builds each entry in a growable `Vec<u8>` (`let mut s: Vec<u8> = Vec::new(); s.extend_from_slice(...)`) and emits via format_entry_string with no length cap, so overlong entries format successfully. Divergence still present; the report's cited lines match main exactly. Report's countercheck verified: value_buf [32]u8 is not a practical bound (u21 max renders "U+1FFFFF", 8 bytes). Not documented as deferred: the only in-file growable-buffer PORT NOTE (value_types.rs:4970) covers Keybinds' RewindBuffer, not this map; DEFERRALS.md fixed-buffer rows (:1006 termio writer, :1853 rustty-os filename) are different surfaces; no clipboard-codepoint-map row in DEFERRALS/MAIN_PARITY/GAP_ANALYSIS. vet.fix_plan: In crates/rustty-config/src/value_types.rs RepeatableClipboardCodepointMap::format_entry (5398-5437): replace the unbounded Vec build with a fixed 1024-byte serialization mirroring the oracle — compose the entry into a [u8; 1024] scratch (prefix "U+{:04X}=" or "U+{:04X}-U+{:04X}=", then the replacement bytes) and on overflow surface the reference's `catch return error.OutOfMemory`. Because Writer::Error is Infallible for the Vec-backed writer (rustty-cfg-fmt/src/writer.rs:22,46) and the crate's locked convention is "OutOfMemory aborts in the Rust port" (value_types.rs:3219), the overflow arm should be a deterministic panic("OutOfMemory") (or a shared buf_print helper returning Result used before the infallible write). Keep the codepoint arm's value_buf semantics (format! is fine — 8 bytes max). Proving test in the same file's mod tests: (a) 1017-byte replacement for a single 4-hex codepoint formats and output is byte-identical to today's; (b) 1018-byte replacement hits the boundary (#[should_panic] or Err, per chosen arm); (c) range-form boundary at 1010 bytes (1024−14). Oracle has no such test — new tests are allowed per task rules.
vet.severity_assessment: Agree with P4 — deterministic fidelity divergence but only reachable with a >1017-byte clipboard replacement string, and Rustty fails "softer" (formats) than Ghostty (errors the dump).
vet.notes: Single-member group; member row = group row. Report is accurate on all cited lines and its boundary math. Fix should be coordinated with the same-family rows W99-B01-01 (font RepeatableCodepointMap, value_types.rs:5240 same growable pattern) and W95-B04-01 (RepeatableStringMap 256-byte buffer) so one shared fixed-buffer helper serves all three; this audit only warrants the clipboard surface.

findings.title: `background-blur` numeric radius parsing accepts malformed underscore placements such as `0x_10`, `_12`, and `12_`, where Ghostty's `std.fmt.parseInt(u8, ..., 0)` rejects them
