findings.title: `clipboard-codepoint-map` replacement codepoints reject Ghostty-accepted `std.fmt.parseInt(u21, ..., 16)` forms such as `+002D` and `00_2D` because Rustty's local parser accepts only raw hex digits
findings.replay_cell: independently found by B01 and upheld by B05; Rustty probe rejected `U++002D`/`U+00_2D`, while Zig `parseInt` oracle accepted the sliced `+002D`/`00_2D` payloads

vet.evidence: Confirmed on current main by close reading. Ghostty oracle (ghostty/src/config/Config.zig:8295-8298): clipboard replacement values starting "U+" slice value[2..] and call std.fmt.parseInt(u21, cp_str, 16). Zig parseInt accepts an optional leading sign and internal '_' digit separators (rejecting leading/trailing '_'); the audit's Zig probe log (.port/codex/evidence/w99-b05-replay/ghostty-oracle.log:5-10) shows +002D=>0x2D, 00_2D=>0x2D, _002D/002D_=>InvalidCharacter, 200000=>Overflow, matching Zig std parseIntWithSign semantics (first/last '_' rejected, other '_' skipped). Rustty current main: crates/rustty-config/src/value_types.rs:5301 routes the same path through parse_int_u21_base16, whose loop (value_types.rs:5447-5470) accepts ONLY [0-9a-fA-F] — '+' and '_' hit the `_ => return Err(Error::InvalidValue)` arm. So "U+0041=U++002D" and "U+0041=U+00_2D" fail in Rustty but parse to 0x2D in Ghostty. Divergence is limited to the replacement-value path: Ghostty's UnicodeRangeParser.parseCodepoint (Config.zig:8160-8185) scans a hex-digit-only slice before calling parseInt, so Rustty's identical-behavior helper at value_types.rs:5642 matches there. Existing Rustty tests (value_types.rs:7746-7763) cover only plain U+002D. No deferral doc covers this (DEFERRALS.md:74 is a formatter note, unrelated).
vet.fix_plan: In /Users/gael/projects/rustty/crates/rustty-config/src/value_types.rs, rewrite parse_int_u21_base16 (line 5447) to mirror Zig std.fmt.parseInt(u21, s, 16) exactly: (1) empty => InvalidValue; (2) optional leading '+' (accept) or '-' (unsigned: only "-0" yields 0, any nonzero digit => InvalidValue, matching Zig Overflow); (3) after sign strip, remainder must be non-empty and must not start or end with '_'; (4) loop skips '_' chars, converts hex digits, errors on other chars; (5) keep the 0x1F_FFFF overflow check. Call sites: value_types.rs:5301 (clipboard replacement — behavioral delta) and 5642 (UnicodeRangeParser — no-op change since input is pre-scanned hex-only, same as Ghostty). Proving tests (add near value_types.rs:7746): parse_cli "U+0041=U++002D" => Codepoint(0x2D); "U+0041=U+00_2D" => Codepoint(0x2D); "U+0041=U+1__0" style doubled separator => ok (0x10); "U+0041=U+_002D", "U+0041=U+002D_", "U+0041=U+200000" => InvalidValue. Run: cargo test -p rustty-config repeatable_clipboard_codepoint_map.
vet.severity_assessment: Agree with P4: obscure Zig-parseInt syntax forms ("+"/"_" in U+hex replacement values) that real configs almost never use; no crash, only stricter rejection.
vet.notes: Report is accurate and still current (code unchanged since audit pin dc054bb). Nuance the report understates: the same helper is also used by UnicodeRangeParser (value_types.rs:5642) but that path is NOT divergent — Ghostty likewise calls parseInt on a pre-scanned hex-digit-only slice (Config.zig:8160-8185), so sign/underscore forms never reach parseInt for range keys; the fix must preserve that (skipping '_' inside the helper cannot change the range path because '_' terminates the scan first). Zig oracle probe line 25 shows doubled internal underscores ("1__0") are accepted by parseInt — the fix should accept them too, matching Zig's skip-'_' loop with only first/last-char rejection.

U++002D, U+00_2D, U+1__0, U+-0 now parse; U+_002D, U+002D_, U+200000, U+-1, U++ reject. The second call site (UnicodeRangeParser, value_types.rs:5834) is unchanged in behavior since it passes a pre-scanned non-empty hex-only slice — matching the oracle at Config.zig:8160-8185.

(2) Zig 0.16.0 /opt/homebrew/Cellar/zig/0.16.0_1/lib/zig/std/meta.zig:657-661: slice arm is "a.ptr == b.ptr and a.len == b.len" — pointer identity, never content. (6) Test gap real too: value_types.rs:7832-7922 has only parse_cli/format tests for this type, no clone/equal assertion (matches W100-B03/B09 supporting rows). Member row W99-B01-03 is the sole member; W100-B03/W100-B09 rows are duplicate/supporting test-contract evidence for it.

(3) face/web_canvas.rs:273-275: `Face::init` forwards those bytes to `init_named` as a CSS "font" string — a self-declared PORT NOTE divergence (:267-272, "the reference web_canvas face has no bytes-based init"). (4) face/web_canvas.rs:547-549: after setting the canvas font, the read-back mismatch check is computed and DISCARDED (`let _ = font_val == check...`), so an invalid binary CSS value succeeds silently with the browser's prior/default font. Oracle: ghostty src/font/face/web_canvas.zig:50 exposes only `initNamed` (no bytes initializer exists), and :312-321 at minimum `log.warn`s "canvas font didn't set" on mismatch; SharedGridSet.zig has no wasm section and is never comptime-instantiated with the web_canvas Face (grep: zero wasm refs), so Ghostty can never reach bytes-as-CSS — Zig would reject it at compile time. Rustty converted that compile-time impossibility into silent runtime fallback and additionally dropped the oracle's warning. Reachability qualification is correct: rustty-web-canvas C ABI does not export SharedGridSet, so the path is latent, public-Rust-library only.
vet.fix_plan: File: crates/rustty-font-shaper/src/face/web_canvas.rs. (a) In `context()` (:547-549), stop discarding the read-back check: log the oracle's warning on mismatch (web_canvas.zig:316-321 parity). (b) In `Face::init` (:273-275), refuse binary payloads instead of silently succeeding: reject sources starting with sfnt/TTC/OTTO/wOFF magic (or any non-UTF8/control bytes) with a new `Error::InvalidFontStr`, and/or have `init_named` fail when the canvas font property did not take, honoring the contract that bytes are never valid CSS. Behavioral delta vs oracle: Ghostty makes bytes-init unrepresentable at compile time; Rustty's shim must at minimum turn it into a loud error, never a silent success on the fallback font. Optionally route the wasm SharedGridSet embedded-fallback arms (shared_grid_set.rs:405-560) to a named CSS fallback ("monospace") under cfg(target_arch="wasm32"). Proving test: extend the existing node probe (wave9-webcanvas-binary-font.mjs pattern) into a repo-checked harness test that feeds JetBrainsMono-Variable.ttf bytes to the release-WASM face constructor and asserts a null/error result plus emitted warning, alongside a `monospace` control that still succeeds; a native unit test can cover the magic-byte rejection of `Error::InvalidFontStr` without wasm.

vet.severity_assessment: Agree with P4: real divergence but latent — no shipped C ABI or demo retains SharedGridSet on wasm; affects public Rust-library users only.
vet.notes: Two corrections/nuances to the report: (1) Ghostty also would NOT hard-fail an invalid CSS font at runtime — its context() only log.warns — so the precise oracle contract is "compile-time unrepresentable + warn on mismatch", not "must fail"; the report's "must not be silently treated as successful" is still fair since Rustty dropped even the warning. (2) The report is otherwise accurate on current main; single-member group, no member-row divergence. The wave-17 B06 pass deliberately did not re-promote W9F-04 (browser-ABI-retention scope), consistent with the latent-reachability qualification.
